item.title: ‘I think that’s cowardice’: Dak Prescott calls it ‘weak’ to blame Brian Schottenheimer
item.description: Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys suffered one of their most painful losses in recent memory on Sunday. And with the heat rising on head coach Brian Schottenheimer, Dak Prescott came to his defense. After the Cowboys blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead and lost to the Arizona Cardinals in overtime, Prescott made it clear he isn’t interested in putting the blame on his coach, calling that “cowardice.” Cowboys’ Collapse The Cowboys led the Cardinals 24-10 early in the fourth quarter on Sunday. But Arizona scored 20 points in the final quarter, including a game-tying touchdown with six seconds left. The Cardinals missed the extra point that would have won it in regulation. But the Cowboys went three-and-out in overtime, and Arizona kicked a field goal to win 33-30. The loss dropped Dallas to 3-5 on the season. Schottenheimer has already faced plenty of criticism this season, with Stephen A. Smith ripping him last month after he called himself a great coach. The latest loss has certainly not calmed the criticism, but Jerry Jones said he isn’t planning to make a coaching change during the season. ‘I Think That’s Cowardice’ During his postgame press conference, Prescott called the loss “one of the toughest” of his career. But he wasn’t going to let Schottenheimer take the fall. “It’s all of us,” Prescott said, via the Cowboys’ official website . “Don’t put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that’s weak. I think that’s cowardice.” Prescott went on to say that winning and losing involves everyone, from the players to the coaches and support staff. “It’s never just one person’s fault. Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it’s never just truly one person’s fault. And so, don’t take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and it’s about us backing him up and backing one another up and we’ll have to show it,” Prescott said. Despite the 3-5 record, the Cowboys aren’t out of it. Nobody in the NFC East has run away with the division, and Prescott said that gives him confidence. “At this point, talk is cheap,” Prescott said. “Telling stories is cheap. We’ve got to go write our own story.” We’ll have to see how the team responds from the loss. The post ‘I think that’s cowardice’: Dak Prescott calls it ‘weak’ to blame Brian Schottenheimer appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Deposits and Withdrawals Due to Ongoing Security Incident, Losses Estimated Near $40 Million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Deposits and Withdrawals Due to Ongoing Security Incident, Losses Estimated Near $40 Million Brazil’s largest cryptocurrency exchange kept deposits and withdrawals suspended on Monday after a security incident in one of its systems. The shutdown left customers unable to send funds into or out of the platform while the company worked to restore operations. Mercado Bitcoin said in a statement posted to X that it had identified and contained the incident. The company said customers suffered no losses and that no data had leaked. It described the suspension as a precaution. Its teams are investigating, tracing assets and coordinating with authorities, the company said. According to Bloomberg, the company said it would absorb all losses. The company has not said which system was breached, how much was taken or when it will reopen. Its current statements gave no total loss figure and no timetable. Mercado Bitcoin has since published destination addresses tied to transactions from the incident, covering Bitcoin, Ethereum-compatible networks, Solana, Stellar and Tron. It said it shared the addresses for identification and tracking purposes. Blockchain security firm Hypernative has put preliminary estimates of suspicious transfers above $40 million across several blockchains. The exchange has not confirmed that figure. Other analysts are citing higher figures and that the sweeping is ongoing. Stablecoin issuer Tether has entered the response. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X at 10:06 a.m. ET that the company had frozen more than 4.5 million USDT linked to the incident. Tether invested $20 million in Mercado Bitcoin back in July, when it said the exchange served 4.5 million users. A rough week for Mercado and other exchanges The incident comes days after one of the largest crypto thefts in recent memory. On Oct. 29, attackers reached $6.3 billion in assets at Binance after compromising an engineer’s laptop and gaining access to internal systems used to process withdrawals. Binance said it found no evidence that private keys were exposed. By Nov. 1, it had replaced 95 percent of the stolen assets and begun restoring withdrawals in phases. On the law enforcement front, the FBI has attributed the attack to North Korea, and the U.S. Secret Service is working with Circle to trace and freeze funds. Tether reported about $1.57 billion in USDT frozen, and Circle said it had frozen more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with authorities. Binance has said it found additional points of breach beyond the initial compromise, which it originally attributed to a single engineer’s laptop. The exchange has not yet published a full post-mortem explaining how the attackers prepared and executed the operation, which some estimates suggest took at least 36 hours of groundwork. item.title: Cubs have 'skeptical' $400 million problem with Tarik Skubal rumor
item.description: Cubs have 'skeptical' $400 million problem with Tarik Skubal rumor originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Cubs are losing nearly their entire starting rotation to free agency. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and trade deadline acquisitions Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes are all unrestricted free agents. That puts Jed Hoyer in a tough spot. This may be the defining offseason of his time as president of baseball operations with the Cubs. If there's one thing Chicago's rotation is missing this offseason, it's an ace. The Cubs could be one of the top landing spots for Tarik Skubal, but are they willing to spend the money? ESPN's Jeff Passan reports the Cubs could shy away from the potentially groundbreaking contract Skubal could secure this winter. "The Chicago Cubs badly want Skubal. They also are skeptical that they will be willing to compete at the sort of dollars Skubal is expected to get -- well in excess of $300 million, potentially in the $400 million-plus range," Passan wrote. There's likely no way of knowing how far the Cubs would be willing to go before backing out of the Skubal sweepstakes. MORE : Dodgers announcer calls for MLB to make major change after Rays' Yandy Diaz check swing controversy Besides Chicago, Passan listed the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets as the top two contenders for the two-time Cy Young Award winner. The Dodgers and Mets are comfortable handing out big contracts. Especially Mets owner Steve Cohen, who signed Juan Soto for $765 million two offseasons ago. Expect to see the Cubs in the mix for Skubal, but they'd be a long shot to land him if they aren't willing to be the highest bidder. item.title: Michigan football sticking with Tommy Carr at QB 'for foreseeable future'
item.description: The Michigan football quarterback carousel has come to a stop. Tommy Carr will start for Michigan (5-3, 2-3 Big Ten) in this weekend's rivalry game against Michigan State (2-6, 0-5) and beyond, coach Kyle Whittingham said at his weekly press conference Monday when he previewed Saturday's matchup (7:30 p.m, Peacock). "Tommy will start this week and for the foreseeable future, unless something changes," Whittingham said. "He played so well, I mean, it's pretty much a given. We haven't had conversation with the team since the game because Sunday's their day off, but we'll cover all that. We'll cover a lot of that ground this morning." Carr comes off the best game of his career and one of the best for a Michigan quarterback in the past three seasons after he completed 22 of 27 passes (81.4%) for 266 yards with one touchdown and no turnovers in U-M's 28-21 win over Rutgers. He was just as effective on the ground, running 12 times for 54 yards and a pair of scores, both of which came in the second half, including a nine-yard scramble on third-and-7 for the game-winning score with 4:24 to play. 'IT'S A DIRTY GAME': Michigan football getting ready for Michigan State rivalry He kept the offense on the field, converting 12 of 16 third downs, and made plays both on time and off schedule. "Liked everything about what he did," Whittingham said. "You talk about QBR, which is an ESPN analytic QB rating that takes into account not just throwing the ball, running the ball, taking sacks, the whole nine yards. He graded out, I think he was 91 or 92, and the top quarterback in the country right now is like 90 or 89. So bottom line is he played a complete game." U-M entered the weekend as the worst passing team in the Power Four conferences, averaging less than 170 yards per game, and Carr exceeded that by nearly 100 full yards. He was 22 of 25 on plays in which he was kept clean, per Pro Football Focus, and handled the blitz well, completing 5 of 6 passes for 81 yards when Rutgers sent extra men. He didn't need the disguise of play-action to get going, completing 14 of 16 passes without the fake-run action for 198 yards, including a seven-yard fade to JJ Buchanan for the first touchdown of the game. He was also 6 of 7 for 105 yards on passes 10 or more yards downfield and picked up 19 total first downs (16 through the air, three on the ground). Michigan has been desperate for consistent play at the quarterback spot and felt it had to move on from former starter Bryce Underwood after he turned the ball over four times in six quarters in the Minnesota game and the first half against Penn State. Carr did commit two giveaways (one fumble, one interception) in a Week 8 loss to Indiana in his first start, but he appeared much more poised in his second start. His performance against Rutgers left little doubt that it was officially his job moving forward. item.title: ‘It Would’ve Been a Great Situation for Him, Wouldn’t It?’ — NFL Legend Revisits Shedeur Sanders’ Missed Chance With Ravens After Lamar Jackson’s Injury
item.description: ‘It Would’ve Been a Great Situation for Him, Wouldn’t It?’ — NFL Legend Revisits Shedeur Sanders’ Missed Chance With Ravens After Lamar Jackson’s Injury Lamar Jackson was back for the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, but the relief was short-lived as the star quarterback picked up another injury, and Baltimore fell 36-10 to the Bills. Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first play, and head coach Jesse Minter later confirmed that the injury will require surgery and send him to injured reserve for at least four games. His backup, Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, stepped in, only to suffer a toe injury of his own in the second quarter, further complicating an already precarious quarterback situation for Baltimore. Shannon Sharpe, however, believes the Ravens may already have missed out on an intriguing solution. On the latest episode of “Nightcap,” Sharpe discussed Baltimore’s depleted quarterback room with Chad “Ochocinco” Johnson and Joe Johnson before revisiting Shedeur Sanders, whom the Ravens reportedly considered drafting in 2025. Shannon Sharpe Points to Shedeur Sanders’ Missed Opportunity “Hey, you think Snoop would be back next week or no?” Ochocinco asked Sharpe. The three-time Super Bowl winner was not optimistic. “No, I doubt it. I doubt it, Ocho. He might be done for the year… That toe, Ocho, that toe bent.” Ochocinco then brought up how slowly turf toe heals, and Sharpe said he knew exactly how long it takes. Then Sharpe circled back to his original thought. “I know a guy that’d been a great situation for,” he started, before Johnson cut in. “Oh, you talking about 2,” Ochocinco said, referring to Sanders and his jersey number. Sharpe confirmed it. “It would’ve been a great situation for him, wouldn’t it?” he said. Sharpe’s comment carried added significance because Sanders reportedly had the opportunity to become a Raven in the 2025 NFL Draft. Baltimore planned to select him with the No. 141 overall pick in the fifth round, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, but Sanders let the team know that he did not want to join a roster with Jackson, where his path to playing time would have been blocked. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The Ravens instead selected offensive lineman Carson Vinson, while Cleveland took Sanders three picks later at No. 144. At the time, avoiding a long-term backup role behind the two-time MVP made sense from Sanders’ perspective. In light of Baltimore’s current injury crisis, however, Sharpe’s point is that the situation looks very different now: had Sanders landed with the Ravens, he could have been in position to compete for immediate playing time with Jackson and Huntley sidelined. Sanders ranked 36th, the third-worst in the league, in Pro Football Network’s QB Impact Ratings last season. He completed 56.6% of his passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions as a rookie. Larson Holds Massive Lead Into NASCAR Finale
item.description: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Kyle Larson sits on the brink of a historic third NASCAR Cup Series title with a commanding 67-point lead. Per Yahoo Sports , the Hendrick Motorsports driver only needs to score nine points at the Homestead-Miami Speedway finale to officially secure the championship. This margin is so large that he does not even need to win the race or lead any laps to take the trophy home. The virtual world is preparing to mirror this real-world drama with the iRacing Homestead Championship Special Event. This week’s sim race covers 400 miles, or 267 laps, on the same track where real drivers will fight for the crown. According to iRacing, the event features dynamic weather and both fixed and open setup options to test driver skill. The Math Makes It Hard For Challengers Christopher Bell and Denny Hamlin face a nearly impossible task to catch Larson before the checkered flag falls. Bell sits in second place but trails by 67 points, while Hamlin is 70 points behind the leader. Per Yahoo Sports, even if Bell scores the maximum 76 points available in the race, Larson would still win the title by reaching that nine-point threshold. This means Larson can finish 28th or better without earning a single stage point and still lock up the championship. The pressure is entirely on his rivals to hope for a mechanical failure or a crash for the No. 5 Chevrolet. Bell finished 10th at Martinsville and Hamlin came in sixth, but neither could close the gap enough to change the odds. William Byron won the Xfinity 500 at Martinsville to jump to ninth in the standings, but he is not in the championship hunt. A pit strategy error that put Larson a lap down early in the race did not stop him from recovering. His ability to get back on the lead lap and finish ninth while holding the points lead shows why he is the favorite to win. Real Life And Virtual Racing Collide The iRacing event is scheduled for November 8 at 3:00 pm ET to match the timing of the real-world finale. According to iRacing, this is the first time since 2019 that Homestead-Miami Speedway will crown the real-world champions for the Cup, Truck, and Xfinity Series. The virtual race uses the current NASCAR Cup Series cars to ensure an authentic experience for sim racers. Shawn Conklin has dominated the iRacing Open season with 25 wins in 49 starts. He holds a lead of nearly 1,700 points over second-place Jacob Reid in the virtual standings. The Fixed Series is much tighter, with Maximillion Bianco leading but Nick Olsen within 200 points of the title. To participate in the special event, drivers must hold a Class C+ or Class D with a 4.0 Safety Rating. The iRacing eSports Network will handle the broadcast call for the top split beginning Friday at 9 pm ET. Fans can watch the action live at iRacing.com/live to see who takes the virtual crown. item.title: Former Penn State wrestling star Levi Haines wins first world title
item.description: Former Penn State wrestling star Levi Haines is a world champion. Could the Biglerville High grade and two-time NCAA individual champ become a Nittany Lion again? Haines won his first world title Sunday in Kazakhstan as part of a stunning display of success by Penn State-affiliated wrestlers at the World Wrestling Championships. Haines won one of three golds and six medals, overall, by Nittany Lion Wrestling Club members in the penultimate (non-Olympic year) freestyle tournament. Haines won his first world title in the 79 kilogram weight class after placing second last season. NLWC members Kyle Snyder (97 kg) and Kyle Dake (86 kg) each won their fifth world titles. PSU sophomore wrestler Marcus Blaze medaled for the first time on the senior world level with a bronze at 61 kg. Former Penn State wrestler Zain Retherford also won bronze at 70 kg. It was a career-defining performance for Haines, who defeated Iran's Mohammad Nokhodilarimi, 4-3, with a winning takedown in the final two minutes. Haines won three decisive matches to open his world wrestling championships run before surviving a 3-3 semifinals finish with Mongolia's Suldkhuu Olonbayar, winning on criteria. What's next for Penn State wrestling's Levi Haines? Haines now remains in limbo following his world title. The rare four-time Big Ten champion continues to wait on whether he will be able to seek a fifth season of eligibility for the Nittany Lions . He's among thousands of former college athletes awaiting a decision in an antitrust lawsuit against the NCAA to determine their eligibility status for the 2026-27 season. Haines is taking classes at Penn State and wishes to compete for a third NCAA title, according to Penn State coach Cael Sanderson , though there's no timeline for the lawsuit ruling. Sanderson recently said Haines is prepared to re-join the Lions' lineup if eligible. "If he gets the call back to folkstyle, he's been wrestling folkstyle his whole life, so he'll be good to go," Sanderson said. The Lions open their dual meet season Nov. 12 against Bloomsburg in Rec Hall. They're riding an 86-match win streak as they begin pursuing their sixth straight NCAA team title. Frank Bodani covers Penn State wrestling for the York Daily Record and USA Today Network. Contact him at fbodani@ydr.com and follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter, @YDRPennState. item.title: Yaxel Lendeborg tags Gabby Williams with Stephen Curry comparison after WNBA Finals MVP
item.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Yaxel Lendeborg tags Gabby Williams with Stephen Curry comparison after WNBA Finals MVP appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams delivered a magnificent performance to secure a 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals. Williams finished with 30 points, 4 blocks, 3 rebounds, 2 assists, and 2 steals, including 15 points and 3 three-pointers in the third quarter and 13 in the fourth. Her performance earned her Finals MVP. Her performance in the WNBA Finals, and specifically in Game 7, drew the attention of Golden State Warriors rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg . Lendeborg attended the game alongside four-time NBA champion and Golden State Warriors starting power forward Draymond Green. “It was awesome,” Lendeborg said of William’s Game 7 performance. “She looked just like Steph Curry, in my opinion. That last game, first half, I think she had 6 points, then you come out in the second half and you just score 20-plus points right away, like 3 back-to-back threes. It was awesome seeing it. It got me going. It felt like I was in the game with her. It was awesome to be able to see that. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lendeborg then showed love to the Golden State Valkyries as an organization. “I’m a big Valkyries fan. As soon as I got drafted here, I’ve been to as many games as I could. It’s a very fun and inspiring environment with the kind of basketball that they play. I mean, next year I’m gonna be right there. First game, front and center.” Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry also showed love to Gabby Williams , taking to his social media to applaud her for the historic victory. “One more for The Bay🏆. Congratulations to all the Valkyries and to Gabby Williams for the Finals MVP! Huge,” Curry posted on his Instagram story.” Related: Stephen Curry pays tribute to Gabby Williams after ‘big time’ WNBA Finals MVP Related: Watch Valkyries get all the love from fans during Warriors-Clippers game

item.title: Aaron Glenn reveals Jets’ stance on Breece Hall situation
item.description: The NFL trade deadline is approaching, and speculation surrounding Breece Hall has intensified following Braelon Allen’s emergence in the New York Jets ‘ backfield. However, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn made it clear Monday that New York has no plans to move on from Hall. Braelon Allen’s emergence has sparked Breece Hall trade speculation. Asked if they’re getting calls on Hall, Aaron Glenn said: "Guys, listen, Breece is still a part of this team. I understand how the noise happens when things like this happen. I’ve said it before, we’re in the business of keeping good players and he’s one of our better players. So Breece will still be here." #Jets — Rich Cimini (@RichCimini) November 2, 2026 Hall has missed five straight games with a quad injury, while Allen has taken advantage of the opportunity. That combination has led to questions about whether the Jets could consider trading Hall before the Nov. 10 deadline. Glenn, however, pushed back firmly on that possibility. MORE: NFL contenders & pretenders after Week 8 Aaron Glenn shuts down Breece Hall trade speculation Sep 27, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; New York Jets running back Breece Hall (20) leaves the game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images When asked whether the Jets have been receiving calls about Hall, Glenn emphasized that the running back remains part of the team’s plans. “Guys, listen, Breece is still a part of this team,” Glenn said. “I understand how the noise happens when things like this happen. I’ve said it before, we’re in the business of keeping good players and he’s one of our better players. So Breece will still be here.” That stance matches what Glenn has said previously about Hall’s role. Before Hall’s latest absence, Glenn said Hall remained the Jets’ starter while Allen would continue to receive opportunities. The Jets are 2-6 after Sunday’s 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, and Hall was inactive for the fifth consecutive game. Glenn said after the loss that Hall was close to returning but that the team wanted to make sure he was fully healthy rather than risk a setback. item.title: Drake Maye provides the answer for shorthanded Patriots in Miami
item.description: The New England Patriots entered the visiting locker room inside Hard Rock Stadium at halftime trailing 13-3 to the one-win Miami Dolphins. It was a sluggish start offensively for a group that was down multiple offensive lineman and three of their top pass catchers before losing tight end Hunter Henry early in the second quarter. It was a sluggish start offensively for a group missing multiple offensive linemen and three of its top pass catchers, before they then lost tight end Hunter Henry early in the second quarter. But the group still had Drake Maye, and that proved to be enough to mount a comeback. “You want to be a great quarterback in the National Football League, there’s not a whole lot of excuses,” head coach Mike Vrabel said post-game. “You go out there and you find ways to win for your football team. And I know that that’s one who he is and that’s what he wants to continue to be. So, he just throws to the open guy and controls our offense and gets guys in the right spot. That’s being one of the best quarterbacks in the league, that’s what the job description requires.” After scoring just three first half points in a rainy Miami, Maye went on to lead three consecutive touchdown drives in the second half to put the Patriots in front. The turnaround began with a 43-yard touchdown pass to Kyle Williams on a deep post, as Maye and the offense began pushing the ball downfield more aggressively. “The touchdown, yeah, I think it was huge. We kind of needed to open it up a little bit and kind of break the barrier of getting in the end zone. I think we did that,” Maye said. “I think Coach was just kind of on us a little bit to stop hurting ourselves, Coach Vrabes and Coach McDaniels. So we were just kind of hurting ourselves and killing drives.” Maye continued to deliver in the second half , capping off the comeback with a two-yard rushing touchdown and a 48-yard touchdown pass to DeMario Douglas. He finished the final two quarters 9-of-10 for 146 yards, with three total touchdowns and a perfect 158.3 passer rating. As Vrabel noted, it was the kind of performance expected from an elite quarterback. With key contributors sidelined and the offense struggling to find its rhythm early, Maye gave the Patriots the spark they needed to leave Miami with a 24-19 victory . “Go be the answer,” Maye said. “Don’t wait around for anybody else, go make it. And I think that was kind of the message everybody took in, and we just felt like we did that. It was good to see from those guys.”

item.title: Brittany Mahomes Trashes Referees Over ‘Weak’ Penalty in Crushing Chiefs Loss
item.description: Brittany Mahomes, Patrick Mahomes Credit: Grant Halverson/Getty; Matthew Stockman/Getty NEED TO KNOW Brittany Mahomes is sharing her opinion about how the Chiefs-Broncos game ended The wife of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes criticized a key call late in the game The Chiefs were called for a false start, negating what would have been a game-winning touchdown and sending them back five yards Brittany Mahomes is taking offense about an officiating call that resulted in a Kansas City Chiefs loss on Sunday, Nov. 1. “You can’t tell me you call that on a game winning TD,” Mahomes, 31, wrote in a post to her Instagram Stories. “Oh wait yeah I can cause it’s us.” She continued, “That’s the weakest call I have ever seen. You can’t tell me otherwise.” The call in question involved her husband Patrick Mahomes , who was moments away from leading the team to a win over the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. But refs called a false start on Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore, just before Mahomes hit Rashee Rice with what would have been the game-winning touchdown pass with four seconds left on the clock. Credit: Brittany Mahomes/Instagram The score was wiped away and the team was backed up five yards — all of which culminated in a clunky play in which the quarterback was sacked by Malcolm Roach and time expired. The Chiefs blew an 11-point fourth quarter lead and lost, 28-24, giving the Broncos the top spot in the division. After the game, Chiefs coach Andy Reid backed up Brittany’s assessment. “I didn’t see it,” Reid told reporters about the call. “That’s one man’s opinion. I just didn’t see it. I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see [a] false start.” The Chiefs now sport a 5-2 record after consecutive losses, having lost to Seattle the week before. Brittany, who has a longstanding practice of defending her husband’s team, called out commentators earlier this season in the Chiefs’ first matchup against the Broncos. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Shortly after they had their way with Denver in the season opener on Monday, Sept. 14, 31-10, she seemingly had the last laugh. “Oopsies,” Brittany wrote on her Instagram Stories that featured a screenshot of four game predictions from ESPN analysts, all of whom picked the Broncos over the Chiefs. Read the original article on People

item.title: Will Mac Jones be a trade target for QB-needy teams?
item.description: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Ian Rapoport, the Baltimore Ravens will look to add help at quarterback after Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that could sideline him for the rest of the season, and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley will miss an extended period with turf toe. That leaves Baltimore with only a QB3. “I do expect the Baltimore Ravens to go out and consider some QB trades, and kinda discuss, ‘How bold do you wanna be?’ Do you want to go out and spend a lot of capital for a quarterback in a season that may be lost because you don’t have Lamar? Or is it going to be a stopgap, and then you end up a seller? These are real decisions that general manager Eric DeCosta and the rest of the Ravens brass.” Rapoport mentioned Tyson Bagent, who was the backup for the Bears under now-Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle last year, as an option. He also brought up Jacoby Brissett, who was benched in Week 8 by the Arizona Cardinals. “There are some options. There aren’t great options, but there are some options out there.” Mac Jones has an expiring contract. He has no ties to Doyle and the Ravens, but he has starting experience and proved he can win last season. The San Francisco 49ers still might value Jones more than those on the outside think they should, given how much they relied on a backup in 2025. It’s a move that doesn’t make sense, but the Vikings, despite their record, are struggling at quarterback. Surprise, surprise: Kyler Murray doesn’t look the part. But why would the 49ers make a playoff contender better? That’s essentially the landscape for quarterback-needy teams in the playoff hunt. It’s slim pickings, and that means Mac Jones is likely here to stay.

item.title: Razorback Report Card: Missouri Postgame
item.description: Oct 31, 2026; Fayetteville, Arkansas, USA; Arkansas Razorbacks running back Cam Settles (27) fumbles a direct snap as Missouri Tigers cornerback Jahlil Florence (21) makes a play for the ball during the first quarter at Donald W. Reyn… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor Arkansas knew the assignment. That makes the final grades harder to excuse. The Missouri pregame report card established specific benchmarks for stopping the run, disrupting Austin Simmons, sustaining the rushing attack, protecting KJ Jackson’s efficiency, and avoiding self-inflicted damage. Those standards were published before kickoff , with an explicit promise not to move them afterward to accommodate the result. Razorback Report Card: Missouri Postgame There is no reason to move them now. Missouri won 34-10, Arkansas fell to 3-5, and a home game following an open date became another examination the Razorbacks could not pass. The Tigers outgained Arkansas 390-288 and converted four turnovers into 24 points. This was not merely a case of a better team winning. Arkansas repeatedly made the better team’s job easier. Run Defense: F The pregame standard required Arkansas to hold Missouri below 150 rushing yards, keep Jamal Roberts below 100, and prevent a rushing gain of 25 yards or more. Those were not arbitrary targets. They addressed the part of Missouri’s offense most capable of controlling the game. Arkansas failed all three measurable tests. Missouri rushed for 211 yards. Roberts finished with 138 on 23 carries, including a 43-yard run that immediately preceded his two-yard touchdown in the third quarter. That sequence illustrated the problem. Following Jackson’s fumble, the defense had an opportunity to limit the damage. Instead, Missouri needed only a brief possession to turn a manageable deficit into a 27-7 game. The turnover created the difficult situation. The defensive response made it decisive. The first-half resistance deserves acknowledgment. Missouri’s offense did not score a touchdown before halftime. But this category measures the complete assignment, not the most encouraging portion of it. Arkansas could not keep the ground game from taking control after the break. Photo Credit: Brett Rojo-Imagn Images Pass Defense: D The pregame requirements included holding Simmons below 60% completions, generating disruption, and limiting explosive passing plays. Arkansas needed to make the quarterback uncomfortable without sacrificing its coverage responsibilities. Simmons completed 20 of 31 passes for 179 yards and two touchdowns. His yardage was modest, but his efficiency cleared the completion threshold Arkansas was supposed to prevent. More importantly, Missouri received a consequential passing play when it needed one. On the opening possession of the third quarter, Simmons found Cayden Lee for 46 yards on third down. The drive ended with a 15-yard touchdown pass to Donovan Olugbode. item.title: 'Crazy' Carrick looks forward to Roma game
item.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick (right) and midfielder Kobbie Mainoo speak to the media before the Champions League match against Roma [Getty Images] Michael Carrick accepts it might sound "crazy" but the beleaguered Manchester United boss says he is looking forward to the Champions League showdown with Roma at Old Trafford. United go into Tuesday's game without a win in nine matches in all competitions. It is their worst run since 1988-89. They have not gone 10 without a win in a single campaign since 1977-78 and there is a growing feeling Carrick will lose his job during the forthcoming international break. Roma's only defeat so far this season was at home to Real Madrid in the Champions League last month, when they led 3-1 with seven minutes left. United are 17th in the Premier League and after defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como have slumped to 21st in the Champions League table after three games, with only the top 24 making it through. It is a bleak backdrop, but rather than fret over what lies ahead, Carrick is viewing it as a chance to change the narrative of the season. "You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but genuinely, I really can't wait for the game," said Carrick. "I'm really looking forward to it. "Listen, I can't look into the future, you never know what's going to happen. That doesn't change the way I feel. Whatever happens is going to happen in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow." Carrick watched over a lively open session of pre-match training at Carrington. Striker Bryan Mbeumo and midfielder Carlos Baleba were particularly vocal, with Argentina defender Lisandro Martinez also fully engaged despite his red card at Chelsea, which triggered such a negative reaction. While there have been calls for Martinez to be dropped for the Roma game, Carrick was more philosophical. "Things happen in football," he said. "Sometimes you do things; you make a decision, you make mistakes. Sometimes it goes well for you." He also dismissed concerns both about Martinez's commitment, and that of his entire squad. "Perceptions are a funny thing," he said. "They can make things look all sorts of different ways. The dressing room is a good place. "I've said it before, I don't question the commitment of the players, to the club and to me and to each other. We need to play better. We can make better decisions. But commitment's not a thing at all." Just need a win - Mainoo Mainoo has scored eight goals in 110 appearances for Manchester United [Getty Images] England midfielder Kobbie Mainoo sat alongside Carrick at the media conference and also stressed the strength of the group. Mainoo returned from a four-match absence with a muscular issue as a second-half substitute at Chelsea. At 21, Mainoo is one of the youngest players in Carrick's squad. item.title: Mike Tomlin sounds off on Cowboys: ‘They’re blinkers. They gotta cut their eyelids off’
item.description: Credit: NBC The Dallas Cowboys suffered an awful, embarrassing home loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. After entering the game as a touchdown favorite and after taking a 10-point lead into the final four minutes of regulation, Dallas proceeded to lose 33-30 in overtime. That’s while Arizona’s backup quarterback Gardner Minshew II stepped in for Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter and completed 17-of-23 passes for three touchdowns and a 137.3 passer rating. https://t.co/XiKd0rrotS — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 1, 2026 It continues a decades-long theme of disappointing Cowboys losses and the team not meeting expectations. And the Cardinals are now 9-1 against the Cowboys since 2008. During halftime of the Sunday Night Football game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Washington Commanders on NBC, Mike Tomlin called out the Cowboys for being “blinkers” and explained that the Cowboys “need to cut their eyelids off.” “I saw a bunch of blinkers… They gotta cut their eyelids off.” Mike Tomlin on the Cowboys after a brutal loss to the Cardinals. https://t.co/HQhKIjYto7 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 2, 2026 “What did you see from the Cowboys?” Football Night in America host Maria Taylor asked Tomlin. “I saw a bunch of blinkers,” Tomlin said. “And what I mean by that- I say, ‘If you’re a blinker, cut your eyelids off.’ What I mean by that is, you gotta relish the thick moments. You gotta want to make the play, as an individual, and as a unit within the team. And watching the end of that game, I didn’t see individuals or particular units that wanted to grab the bull by the horns and win the game.” “Certainly, their defense; we can spend a lot of time talking about that two-minute drive and things of that nature,” Tomlin continued. “But their offense had a short field when [the Cardinals] had an unsuccessful onside kick at the end of regulation, and then they went three-and-out in overtime. And so, I see a team that doesn’t have anybody that wants to be the unit to secure victory. They’re blinkers. They gotta cut their eyelids off.” “Well, let me ask you this,” Taylor responded. “If you see that type of team, as a coach, what can you do to reorient them to move forward in the season? Because it’s not all lost; it’s the NFC East.” “You gotta figure out who wants it, and you gotta shift your division of labor to those that want it,” Tomlin explained. “And so, knowledge of your team is a major component. But also, you gotta challenge those guys, individually and collectively. Tell ’em you’re looking for that guy, and who wants to be it?” Tomlin knows what winning football looks like after leading the Pittsburgh Steelers to a .628 winning percentage and a Super Bowl title over 19 seasons as the organization’s head coach. And he’s used that knowledge to deliver very honest commentary in his first year as an NFL analyst for NBC. Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer has a lot to figure out. item.title: What was Kimi Antonelli’s best moment of his F1 title-winning campaign? Our writers have their say
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli ’s record-breaking Formula 1 world championship triumph was highlighted by many superb performances. But which one was his best? Antonelli duly wrapped up his maiden F1 crown in Mexico with four rounds to spare – becoming the youngest-ever world champion in the process. Our writers have picked out the moments they believe turned the Italian from a contender into a world champion in waiting. Melbourne crash response offered first glimpse of new Kimi – Filip Cleeren Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes It may sound odd to pick one of Antonelli's few defeats against Russell, but his runner-up spot to the Briton at the season opener in Melbourne showed me the first tranche of evidence that the Antonelli who had rocked up Australia wasn't the same insecure rookie who had struggled through spells of 2025. The Albert Park weekend was actually one of Antonelli's more challenging weekends, suffering a heavy 25G crash in FP3 that looked set to derail his weekend. It may have done a year prior, but this time the young Italian stayed cool and collected. And as Mercedes was able to pull off a full rebuild just in time for qualifying, Antonelli was able to shake off the incident and take second on the grid behind Russell despite not being able to finetune the car's set-up. In the race Antonelli then suffered from a poor getaway with no battery power as he was swamped and dropped to sixth, but Mercedes' pace advantage was thus that he was able to make a controlled recovery to second. "If something like that had happened to me last year, the rest of the weekend would probably have been very compromised," Antonelli reflected in Austin. "When you have one year of experience, one full year in Formula 1, you come back the next year and you just feel better. Things happen a bit more easily, let's say, also because you're not forcing them to happen as much. "I kind of took a step back in that regard and just tried to focus on the important things and enjoy the process as much as possible. Definitely, mentally I've been in a much happier place this year compared to last season. And especially when you've been working with the same group of people for one year, going into year two is a big difference as well. You know how to move on together as a team, especially from difficult situations." Canadian GP - Antonelli's real statement drive – Ewan Gale Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes By the time F1 had rocked up to the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve, Antonelli had already proven that he possesses some of the traits needed to be successful. Yet this was the first real ding-dong battle we had seen between the Italian and an adversary that meant something. Fighting for the lead with Russell throughout the first half of the race, we saw that Antonelli was not going to be a pushover for his more experienced team-mate in the race for the title.

item.title: Carrick shrugs off Man Utd sack talk ahead of Roma match
item.description: Michael Carrick brushed off suggestions he has just two games left as Manchester United boss as he prepares his underperforming side for Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Roma. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford is increasingly precarious following Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, which extended United’s winless run in all competitions to nine games — they last had a longer such sequence in 1984. Former United and England midfielder Carrick was asked at his pre-match press conference on Monday whether he felt he had just two games remaining at the helm — against Roma and Aston Villa. The Villa match on Sunday comes just before an international break, potentially giving the United hierarchy an opportunity to make a managerial change. “No, not at all,” said the 45-year-old, in his first full season in charge. “If you look into the future, you never know what’s going to happen. “I don’t know what’s going to happen. That doesn’t change the way I feel, how we’re preparing for the game tomorrow. “I’m actually really looking forward to the game, can’t wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I’m crazy with the results we’ve had and what’s going on, but I genuinely can’t wait.” Carrick also said he had “no concerns” over the commitment of out-of-form Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez, who was sent off in United’s defeat at Stamford Bridge. The defender had previously criticised club chiefs over a lack of investment in the squad. “Things happen in football, sometimes you do things, sometimes you make decisions, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but the commitment is not an issue for sure,” said Carrick. – Dressing-room mood – The United head coach insisted the dressing room was in “a good place” despite the club’s terrible start to the season. “Perception is a funny thing. You can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things,” he said. “I’ve said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don’t question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment is not a thing at all.” United are just one place above the Premier League relegation zone after taking a mere seven points from their nine matches so far this season. And they are 20th in the Champions League table following a dismal 4-1 defeat away at Como last month. Only the top 24 teams will progress beyond the league phase. But midfielder Kobbie Mainoo, sitting alongside Carrick at Monday’s press conference, said United could turn things around. “We’ve not had the results we’ve wanted,” said the 21-year-old. “But we need to look forward now. There’s big, big games ahead and I feel like we’re one win away from changing that.” Carrick has fond memories of facing Roma as a member of Alex Ferguson’s team, scoring twice in United’s 7-1 quarter-final second-leg triumph in the Champions League in 2007. “It was a magical night, I have to say,” he recalled

Why Xabi Alonso is “happy for” player who takes “so many right decisions”
item.description: Why Xabi Alonso is “happy for” player who takes “so many right decisions” Xabi Alonso has been signing the praises of Romeo Lavia, the midfielder who was excellent against Man U on Saturday. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Xabi Alonso had a few players to praise after Saturday’s big win over Manchester United. Morgan Rogers got a decisive goal and Mike Penders made a crucial save. But in the end Alonso focused his praise on Romeo Lavia, who was great in midfield and completed 90 minutes for the Blues just days after doing so for the first time in a competitive game on Wednesday night. Alonso “very happy” for Lavia Xabi Alonso on his team’s win over Man U. “He has done so many things right. He was always connecting the defence with the attacking players, he was able to switch the game, he has taken many right decisions, was very dynamic and competitive,” Alonso said post-game. “So I think, not just this game but in the last two or three weeks, he has been playing at a very good level and I’m very happy for him.” Despite proving his fitness since the start of the season, Lavia had actually been out of Alonso’s regular first team once Henderson was fit. It will be a very hard decision between them going forward – Lavia has more quality on the ball, but Alonso clearly loves the leadership and intangibles that Henderson brings. We’re curious to see what team we see on Sunday. In other news… Morgan Rogers was decisive again on Saturday – but says he still wants to improve one part of his game in particular.

item.title: Join us for the 2026-27 St. John’s basketball season on the SB Nation app
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 22: Head coach Rick Pitino of the St. John's Red Storm celebrates a 67-65 victory against the Kansas Jayhawks after the game in the second round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Viejas Arena at San Diego State University on March 22, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Almost two months ago, we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. The app is available in North America, and we’re working on Europe and the rest of the world as we speak! Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past seven weeks and have been using it, but if you are a big college basketball fan, it’s also entirely possible a few of you missed it! The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center. One of the most exciting new features is the game chat, which some of you may have already test-driven during the preseason. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games, and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you’re not going to find anywhere else. We also wanted to elevate the community’s contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we’ve set single-day commenting records three different times in the last several weeks. And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there’s an option at the top to do that. So, thanks for making us part of your routine. If you haven’t checked it out, you can get the app for iOS or Android . And if you’re not an app user, that’s OK! We’re glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable. College hoops fans, game day is better on the SB Nation app! React to every crossover, alley-oop, and block alongside fellow basketball fans in real time. Join the live game chat Spend less time looking at ads Jump seamlessly between communities Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

item.title: Jamie Carragher defends Madueke over Mac Allister incident
item.description: Jamie Carragher defends Madueke over Mac Allister incident Jamie Carragher has expressed his frustration with Alexis Mac Allister’s reaction during Liverpool’s encounter with Arsenal, after the midfielder appeared to exaggerate an incident involving Noni Madueke in an attempt to get the Gunners player sent off. Mac Allister was one of Liverpool’s most involved players during the match, frequently getting on the ball and attempting to create opportunities for his team. The Argentine midfielder, like several of his teammates, was frustrated by Arsenal’s defensive resilience and struggled to find a way through their organised backline. Liverpool were desperate to find a breakthrough and had also been hoping to receive a penalty during the contest. However, they could potentially have benefited from having an Arsenal player dismissed as well, making the incident between Mac Allister and Madueke particularly significant. Carragher unhappy with Mac Allister’s reaction The two players came together during the match, with their heads making contact. Mac Allister subsequently went to ground, raising the possibility that Madueke could receive a red card for the incident. Although similar situations can sometimes result in a dismissal, Carragher felt the contact was too soft to justify such punishment. The pundit was particularly unimpressed by the Liverpool midfielder’s reaction, despite his strong connections with the Merseyside club as a former player and supporter. Rather than defending his former club’s player, Carragher backed Madueke and criticised the growing tendency among footballers to exaggerate contact in an attempt to influence refereeing decisions. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Carragher defends Arsenal winger The pundit made his feelings clear when discussing the incident, insisting that players should be held accountable for such behaviour. Speaking about the confrontation, he said, as reported by Give Me Sport : “I’m delighted he never got sent off there. We have got to be strong on calling people out and saying that this is embarrassing. I can’t stand it. “I think everybody in the country watching football this head-to-head stuff. If someone puts their head back and butts, of course it’s a red card, but this stuff about head-to-head and if someone touches, the other one goes down and the player gets sent off.” Carragher’s comments highlight his frustration with exaggerated reactions and attempts to influence refereeing decisions. He believes genuine violent conduct should result in punishment, but minimal contact should not lead to an unnecessary dismissal. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. You agree not to give any personal abuse to other Arsenal fans. Everyone is allowed to hold their own opinions even if you disagree with them. It COSTS NOTHING TO BE POLITE TO OTHER ARSENAL FANS. item.title: Stat of the Day: Mercedes Needs Only a 3-Point Edge on Ferrari in Brazil to Clinch the Constructors’ Title
item.description: Photo by Jonathan Borba on Pexels.com Mercedes leads Ferrari 630 points to 504 with four Formula 1 rounds left. That 126-point gap looks like a runaway, and it is. The number that matters this week is smaller: three . That is how many points more than Ferrari Mercedes must score in the São Paulo Grand Prix to lock up the constructors’ championship at Interlagos. The math behind the stat A team can score a maximum of 43 points in a grand prix: 25 for a win and 18 for second place. There are no sprint races left, because all six 2026 sprint weekends (Shanghai, Miami, Montréal, Silverstone, Zandvoort and Singapore) are done. The remaining rounds are São Paulo (November 6-8), Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Once Brazil is over, three races will remain, so Ferrari’s ceiling is 3 x 43 = 129 points. If Mercedes leaves Interlagos 129 or more points clear, Ferrari cannot pass it. From a 126-point lead, Mercedes only needs to outscore Ferrari by three. A tie on points would also go to Mercedes on wins, which it leads 12 to 2 this year. What it reveals competitively Three points is a small ask. Mercedes has averaged about 33.2 points per round against Ferrari’s 26.5, a margin of roughly 6.6 per race. The target for Brazil is less than half of its normal edge. For Ferrari to stop the clinch it would need to beat Mercedes by four or more in a single non-sprint race, which in practice means a near-perfect Sunday with Mercedes stumbling at the same time. The split inside the points explains why. Mercedes’ 630 is Kimi Antonelli’s 380 plus George Russell’s 250. Ferrari’s 504 is Lewis Hamilton’s 259 plus Charles Leclerc’s 245. Russell and the Ferrari pair are within a few points of one another; Antonelli is the whole gap . He has won nine of Mercedes’ 12 races, while Ferrari has taken just two wins between its drivers. We broke down his title run in our earlier look at his points lead and his one-stop win in Austin . Photo by Jonathan Borba on Pexels.com Why the clinch matters beyond the trophy The constructors’ standings are where the money is. Final positions set the share of Formula 1’s prize fund, which we explained in how the constructors’ championship determines prize money . Mercedes had already been in the frame to take both crowns, as covered in Mercedes Can Win Both F1 Titles in Mexico City . Antonelli’s drivers’ title is secured, so Brazil is now about whether the team side can be closed out with three races still to run. What to watch in Brazil Ferrari’s one-two ceiling: only a Hamilton-Leclerc double podium combined with a Mercedes weak day keeps the title alive past Interlagos. Russell’s Sunday: Antonelli will score, so Russell’s finish decides whether Mercedes gets there comfortably. The fallback dates: if Brazil does not do it, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi each cut Ferrari’s maximum by another 43. item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Jonathan Loáisiga
item.description: BRONX, NY - JULY 29: New York Yankees Pitcher Jonathan Loaisiga (43) delivers a pitch during the seventh inning of a Major League Baseball game between the Tampa Bay Rays and the New York Yankees on July 29, 2025, at Yankee Stadium in The Bronx, NY. (Photo by Gregory Fisher/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Everybody loves the big-name acquisition, but sometimes, the small, unheralded move that pays dividends can be a real difference maker for a ballclub. On February 6, 2016, the Yankees made one such move, signing minor league free agent Jonathan Loáisiga after he was cut by the San Francisco Giants, as they sought to add pitching depth to the farm system during a transitory period in the organization’s history. The man who would come to be known as “Johnny Lasagna” would go on to fill a critical role in the Yankees’ bullpen during the 2021 season, before injuries ultimately robbed him derailed his Yankees career. Jonathan Stanley Loáisiga Estrada Born: November 2, 1994 (Managua, Nicaragua) Yankees Tenure: 2018-2025 Born and raised in Nicaragua, Loáisiga signed as an international amateur free agent with the San Francisco Giants on September 23, 2012. He made his professional debut the following season, going on to make 13 appearances with the DSL Giants. Although his performance was encouraging — he had just a 2.75 ERA and 1.107 WHIP in that span — his Giants career was effectively over after that; injuries robbed him of the entire 2014 and 2015 seasons, and as a result, the Giants cut him loose. As noted above, Loáisiga signed with the Yankees that winter, and was assigned to Single-A Charleston (the Yankees cut ties with them during the 2020-2021 restructuring, and they are now a member of the Rays family). Immediately, the injury woes followed the young right-hander: just 2.1 innings into his first start he tore his UCL and underwent Tommy John surgery. Unlike the Giants, though, the Yankees were willing to be patient, and added him to the 40-man roster in 2017 in order to protect him from the Rule 5 Draft (something they did not do with Garrett Whitlock a few years later). When he returned to the mound with the GCL Yankees that summer, Loáisiga rewarded that faith. He flew through the farm system, and by the middle of the 2018 season, when the Yankees needed a spot starter in June, they recalled him straight from Double-A Trenton — bypassing the entire Scranton RailRiders roster. Making his MLB debut at Yankee Stadium against the Tampa Bay Rays, Loáisiga rose to the challenge, striking out six in five scoreless innings to earn his first major league win. He would make three more starts before being sent down to make his Scranton debut, posting an even 3.00 ERA and allowing just one home run in that span. item.title: Jerry Koosman, dead at 83
item.description: NEW YORK, NY - UNKNOWN: Jerry Koosman #36 of the New York Mets poses for a photo with Jerry Koosmans Big Bite Fan Club prior to a National League game on an unknown date at Shea Stadium in the Queens borough of New York City. (Photo by Louis Requena/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Yesterday, the baseball world learned of the passing of Jerry Koosman, a member of both the 1969 World Champion and 1973 National League Champion New York Mets, at 83 year old. Koosman, a member of the Mets Hall of Fame and whose number 36 is retired by the Mets, is one of the most identifiable Mets from their first golden era. Born in Appleton, Minnesota, the left-hander was discovered while in the military, and the Mets signed him one his service was over. He made his big league debut in 1967, but joined the Mets full time in 1968, going 19-12 with a 2.08 ERA and 178 strikeouts in 263.2 innings. Koosman finished second to Johnny Bench in the Rookie of the Year voting. In 1969, Koosman had another fantastic season, and won two games in the ‘69 World Series, pitching 17 and two-thirds innings over two games, and was awarded the ball Cleon Jones caught for the final out of the game. Koosman continued to be the Mets’ number two starter behind Tom Seaver, and he had a number of very good seasons as Met, including winning 21 games in 1976 and coming in second in the Cy Young voting in 1976. After the Mets’ terrible 1978 season, Koosman requested a trade and was traded to the Twins in exchange for Greg Field and, as a player to be named later, fellow Mets legend Jesse Orosco. Over his 12 year Mets career, Koosman put up a 3.07, with a 140-137 record. He was an All-Star in 1968 and 1969. After a fantastic year in 1979 for the Twins, Koosman’s career never quite hit those high marks again. After two and a half seasons with the Twins, two and a half for the White Sox, and two for the Phillies, Koosman retured after the 1985 season. He ended his career with 53.6 bWAR. Koosman has the third most pitching wins in Mets history (140), behind teammate Seaver and Dwight Gooden. The Mets inducted him into their Hall of Fame in 1989 and retired his number in 2021. He was just the third Met player to have his number retired. Koosman is survived by three children and four grandchildren.

item.title: Dodgers Breakout Star Projected to Crack MLB Roster in 2027
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have to change something before next season begins following their disappointing finish to the 2026 season, and Sonja Chen of MLB.com believes an extended run of games for Josue De Paula could go a long way. In her “way-too-early” look at the Dodgers’ roster for 2027 , Chen listed De Paula as the Dodgers’ starting left fielder. Why Would the Dodgers make Josue De Paula Their Starting Left Fielder? De Paula only has 11 regular-season MLB games under his belt, but looked like a seasoned player during his brief tenure in the bigs last season. He hit a monster home run against the Miami Marlins during those 11 games, bringing home a total of seven runs while posting a 1.081 OPS with a .500 on-base percentage. His performances during the regular season earned him a spot on both the NLDS and NLCS roster. Sep 13, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers left fielder Josue de Paula (95) rounds the bases after hitting a three-run home run against the Miami Marlins during the fourth inning at loanDepot Park. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images De Paula only featured four times in the postseason, stepping up to the plate three times, and drew one walk. “The outfield is a chance for the Dodgers to mix things up, although their three starters in 2026 — Teoscar Hernández, Pages and Tucker — are all under contract in ’27,” Chen wrote . “De Paula, L.A.’s top prospect and No. 4 overall per MLB Pipeline, certainly looked the part of a big league hitter in 11 games in September. But his defense remains a big question mark.” De Paula played well beyond his years in 2026, and giving him a shot in the majors next season would be a borderline criminal offense by the Dodgers. What is the Case Against Josue De Paula Starting? While his offensive capabilities are impressive and he almost certainly deserves a spot on the roster, starting as the Dodgers’ left fielder may be too much too soon for the rookie. As Chen stated, the organization has concerns over his defense in the outfield, and have made clear they want to see improvement from him. “I think with [De Paula], we’ve talked through it and he’s fully aware of continuing to improve defensively,” general manager Brandon Gomes said . “We’ve all seen what he’s capable of in the box which is incredibly exciting. With that being said, we have a very talented core group already here, so I think it’s finding those opportunities but also making sure that throughout this offseason and coming into spring training that he continues to improve and get to that bar and gets to be an above average defender.” Additionally, having De Paula in the lineup gives the Dodgers another left-handed bat in an already lefty-heavy lineup. Other than De Paula, the Dodgers have Max Muncy, Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Kyle Tucker as left-handed bats. item.title: Should the Saints be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline?
item.description: The season for the New Orleans Saints has not gone as the organization had planned so far, and coming off a bye week, the Saints are in a very precarious situation. As the division stands right now, the Saints are only one game out of first place. Every other team has three wins, with the Panthers, who have already had their bye week, sitting at four losses while the rest of the division has five. This puts the Saints in a difficult situation. Do they make a move at the trade deadline to try to go all in and win the division, or do they punt on the 2026 season because of the systemic issues and the need to acquire more young talent on cheap contracts for the long-term challenges ahead? Looking at the roster as it stands right now, if the Saints wanted to bring in some players to help them win, they would have to spend future draft capital on the defensive side of the ball. The Saints spent the entire offseason ignoring some major issues on defense, especially their inability to stop the run. They would have to start there, focusing on the line of scrimmage. The first player to explore would be Grover Stewart, the interior defensive tackle for the Colts. Stewart is one of the best run-stuffing tackles in the league. During his NFL career, he has recorded over 400 total tackles and 13 sacks. The issue with Stewart is that he has now been in the league for nine years. Do you feel comfortable with the Saints sending draft capital in exchange for a veteran who has been in the league this long? Other options include Daron Payne of the Commanders, an eight-year veteran who can defend the run and add valuable interior pass-rushing ability, with 38 sacks over his career, and Dalvin Tomlinson. Tomlinson is not as accomplished as Payne and Stewart, but he is a player known for his play and durability. He has not missed a start over his nine-year career, and on a team that struggles with health issues, this would be an immediate upgrade. The Saints could also look at linebackers like Cody Barton of the Titans and Daiyan Henley of the Chargers. But at this point, the Saints should not be comfortable giving up draft capital in a season like this one. This is not a team that is just a single player away from making a run. It’s one thing to consider going on a championship run with the playoffs in sight, but this team is trying to make a run to win a poor division. This is a team trying to make a run to win eight or nine games. This is not an acceptable position to be in when it comes to trading away future assets just to finish a season with fewer than double-digit wins. As the trade deadline approaches, the Saints may want to consider trading players to acquire more assets. But the issue is that the Saints don’t really have a roster constructed in a way that could bring back a haul like the Titans just received, which included two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick. item.title: Winners, Losers, & Honorable Mentions in UNC’s failed upset bid against Miami
item.description: CHAPEL HILL, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 24: Running back Demon June #0 of the North Carolina Tar Heels celebrates with tight end Jelani Thurman #45 of the North Carolina Tar Heels after scoring a touchdown in overtime of their game against the Syracuse Orange at Kenan Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. (Photo by Matt Kelley/Getty Images) | Getty Images One thing you will not see out of this post is a discussion of the officiating, let’s go ahead and get that out of the way from the start. Yes, we can argue about the pass interference call or the flags on the onside kicks, but anyone who’s been around since the 2015 loss to Clemson in the ACC Championship knows real injustice. Besides, Carolina scored on the PI call anyway, and they shouldn’t have gotten to where they needed the onside kicks. THAT is something you will see. There’s time later to talk about the program in the macro — where it’s going, just how successful it is being led by a coach whose clock is ticking — but in the micro you can’t help but to admire the turnaround this program has made from last season to this. This is coming from someone who still thinks they need a different coach, by the way. The important thing now is to not let this be the high point of the season. With that, let’s talk about our winners, losers, and honorable mentions from the very narrow 38-35 loss to The U. Winners Jelani Thurman – Five catches, two touchdowns, and one of those being a spectacular catch on a great play by Billy Edwards, Jr. At this point in the season you run out of superlatives to talk about just how great an addition this was. You’d be excused for thinking his play early in the season was a mirage and wondering just how well he’d do as defenses keyed in on him. Well, we have our answer. This was, without a doubt, the biggest stage that Thurman will have all season and he shined in front of a national audience. He’s draft eligible after this year and so he’s going to have a great decision to make between some real NIL money or heading pro. Either way, the family should send some thanks to Bobby Petrino. Billy Edwards, Jr – It was the best game of his career, and it wasn’t particularly close. He played the type of game you wanted from a sixth-year player, and executed the gameplan almost flawlessly. His reads were on point, he kept exploiting the Miami defense, and he — along with Petrino — may have just given game film for the rest of college football on how to exploit this Hurricanes defense. We’ll get to the bad in a second, but the Tar Heels are not in this game without the steady hand of Edwards. Anytime you can throw for 341 yards and four touchdowns against the number one team in the country, it’s a good night. Against any other team, Edwards probably earns them a win. item.title: Fulton’s Gavin Doty ‘counting down the minutes’ to Syracuse debut
item.description: Gavin Doty #4 of the Syracuse Orange is introduced in the starting lineup before the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame college basketball exhibition game between the Syracuse Orange and the UConn Huskies at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, United States, on October 13, 2026. (Photo by Erica Denhoff/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images SYRACUSE, N.Y. — Growing up in nearby Fulton, wearing the Syracuse Orange uniform was a lifelong dream for Gavin Doty. On Monday, he’ll do so as he takes the floor of the JMA Wireless Dome for the first time as a member of his hometown team. Syracuse opens the regular season against New Haven, the first game of the Gerry McNamara era. He’s been looking forward to this for a while. “I’m so excited, man,” Doty said on Syracuse men’s basketball media day on October 9. “I can’t wait. I’m counting down the minutes. That November 2nd game is gonna feel quite special.” If McNamara could create a player in a lab to play for him, it would look a lot like Gavin Doty. He basically said as much after Siena won the MAAC Championship last March, saying he’s as close, in terms of competitiveness, to himself as any player he’d ever coached. Loyal, local, and laborious, he came to Siena as a young freshman two seasons ago after playing 17U EYBL for Albany City Rocks over the summer. He was considering taking a prep year, but decided to attend Siena and play for McNamara. Doty made impressions in practices leading up to that 2024-25 season, McNamara’s first as a head coach. “By the third day,” McNamara said after winning the MAAC Championship. “He was everywhere. I was like ‘jeez, he’s gotten like five offensive rebounds every day in this segment’.” Yet, he didn’t start the year in the rotation, as the Saints relied on veteran guards. He quickly made it known that he would need to be part of the mix. By January, he entered the starting lineup. A few weeks later, he was in Rookie of the Year talks. There was no adjustment period. “I watched him go from sixth man to starter to arguably the best and most consistent player in the league in the span of five weeks his freshman year,” McNamara said on media day. He didn’t take home Rookie of the Year, nor would he take home Player of the Year as a sophomore. But the trophy he did win means more. Doty was the MVP of the MAAC Tournament, leading the Saints to victory over Merrimack in the championship game. He then scored 21 points against Duke in Siena’s near-upset of the Blue Devils the next week. McNamara left for the Syracuse job, and it was a foregone conclusion who his first commitment would be. “There was no thought at all,” Doty said. “I didn’t even think about going anywhere else. I’m sure people were trying to get after me, but I was really just focused on helping GMac get this program back.” Doty averaged 18 points and 6.9 rebounds per game for the Saints last season.
