item.title: How new wrinkles are helping Mizzou evolve its rushing attack
item.description: Oct 31, 2026; Fayetteville, Arkansas, USA; Missouri Tigers wide receiver Damarion Fowlkes (3) runs the ball during the second quarter against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Rojo-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mizzou took a unique approach on a 4th and 1 with several potential ball carriers against Arkansas’ defense. Austin Simmons lined up in the gun, with Jamal Roberts aligned to his left. Simmons simply could’ve just handed it off to Roberts. But with the play clock going under 15 seconds, Simmons sprinted under center, with Roberts aligned off the left tackle. DeMarion Fowlkes finished his motion by aligning the offset of Jordon Harris. A quarterback sneak with a 6-foot-4 Simmons is another option, but instead, it’s Fowlkes taking the ball on a jet sweep. The 5-foot-9 wide receiver made one cut before muscling his way for a six-yard gain. Seven plays later, Blake Craig nailed a 53-yard field goal, extending the Tigers’ lead to 13-0, on their way to a 34-10 win. Going back to the jet sweep to Fowlkes, it’s something that we haven’t seen from the Tigers’ offense much this season. But it was frequent on Saturday as it gave gave Arkansas more rushing threats to defend on top of playing against one of the best running backs in the SEC. At that point in the second quarter, that was Fowlkes’ third designed rushing attempt of the night. He was the only wide receiver to have a rush attempt this season prior to Saturday with one. But Cole Cubelic noted on the broadcast how Chip Lindsey was using the east-west game a lot to generate quick touches for Mizzou’s playmakers. The offense ran a handful of screens, while Fowlkes produced in the rushing attack. On his first attempt, off Trajen Greco’s interception, Fowlkes picked up eight yards on a jet sweep. The second, Mizzou lined up under center, Fowlkes went in motion and followed the blocks of Harris and Jude James for a four-yard gain. In the postgame, when describing an improvement in the red zone, Drinkwitz highlighted how staying ahead of the chains leads to better play calls. Applying that same principle, Fowlkes’ carries created more manageable situations for Mizzou, producing a 2nd and 2 and 3rd and 5. The following plays from both rushes were a six-yard gain by Roberts and a Simmons completion to Olugbode for a first down. Jet sweeps aren’t the only thing that’s been developing in within MU’s offense. Over the past three games in SEC play, the Tigers have leaned a bit into Simmons’ potential as a running threat. Mizzou has called three quarterback draws over the past three games, two to end the half against Texas A&M, and another at Ole Miss. Against Arkansas, it was called once again. On a 2nd and 1, Mizzou lined up four receiving options near the hash marks or wider, with Olugbode lined up by himself near the numbers, creating a five-wide set. It creates a lighter box for Arkansas, as it has to allocate resources out wide

item.title: Phillies Report Card: Otto Kemp
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 01: Otto Kemp #31 of the Philadelphia Phillies strikes out to end the game against the Atlanta Braves in game three of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park on October 01, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Edward M. Pio Roda/Getty Images) | Getty Images Against Chris Sale, with two outs in the ninth inning of game three of the National League Wild Card in Atlanta, Otto Kemp ended the Phillies season by swinging right over a slider. Believe it or not, the Phillies had real hopes for Otto Kemp heading into 2026. He put up a .786 OPS against left-handed pitching in 2025, roughly 20% above league average, believe it or not. Kemp notably played through a fractured left kneecap and he needed surgery on his shoulder after the 2025 season. He clearly checked the intangible boxes and showed some real ability at the plate. He slugged .411 with a 92 OPS+ as a rookie and did not look incompetent against right-handed pitching most of the time. Dave Dombrowski clearly liked what he saw, insisting he thought Kemp could turn into an everyday player but they settled on the short-side platoon LF spot. He was never a good defender but he wasn’t completely unathletic and should hit lefties. Sounds like a perfectly acceptable platoon partner for Brandon Marsh, right? Nope. It was a disaster. What went right? Kemp made the opening day roster and the Phillies came into the season with him in mind so clearly something went fine in spring training, at least enough so the Phillies could maintain the course. What went wrong? After going 2 for 20 with nine strikeouts, a walk, and a hit-by-pitch, not to mention he was a disaster in left field, Kemp was optioned in the middle of the Phillies 10 game losing streak. Felix Reyes came in his place, hit a home run off Chris Sale but nothing else and would later get optioned. Kemp would find himself back in the big leagues a month after his option, with another chance to prove he could platoon with Brandon Marsh in left field. He played in three more games, getting five at bats and didn’t record a hit. With Marsh on a linsanity run against left handed pitchers, there was no place for Otto Kemp on the roster and he would not play for the Phillies for four months. Until October, Kemp was put on the Phillies playoff roster after a rash of minor league injuries to end the season. The 2026 Phillies postseason roster for their series against the Atlanta Braves included Kemp, Rafael Marchán and Garrett Stubbs, along with Tanner Banks and Chase Shugart in the bullpen. Not that you would need to find a role for all 26 players in a three game series, but that is an insane amount of dead weight going into October. Kemp would play when Don Mattingly hit him for Brandon Marsh against Chris Sale. It was supposed to be this way heading into the season and it would be the way the season ended. Kemp had no chance on a backfoot slider and the Phillies went home empty handed. Final Grade: D- Does Kemp deserv

item.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake beats South Glens Falls for its 4th straight Section 2 Class B field hockey title
item.description: Burnt Hills celebrates after defeating South Glens Falls to win the Section 2 Class B championship on Sunday at Glens Falls High School. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) GLENS FALLS - When Grace Kogut and Katie Lansley were eighth graders on the 2022 Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake field hockey team, their first varsity season ended in devastation. That 2022 season ended the Spartans' run of nine consecutive Section 2 Class B championships. In the years since, Kogut and Lansley have been key contributors for the program, as it's begun a brand new stretch of dominance. On Sunday afternoon, Burnt Hills defeated South Glens Falls 6-1 to secure its fourth straight Class B championship. "A little bit, but I'm very confident in our team," Kogut, now a senior, said on whether she ever gets flashbacks from the championship game loss in 2022, which came against South Glens Falls. "Today we were ok, but there's definitely some bad memories there. "At least for me, I feel like after that loss, we wanted to push to get better. It was heartbreaking and I know we never wanted to feel like that again." In addition to Burnt Hills' four straight Section 2 titles, the Spartans are two-time defending Class B state champions and are set to return to the state tournament looking to defend their crown. "We're really proud of the team to get it up to four. Even though we had so many before and we lost (in 2022), it's really good to see us build it back up," Lansley said. "I think it's the team culture, and we're a family. We carry that on to the field. Every year, the team is so close on and off the field, and I feel like that really carries us." Burnt Hills' Katie Lansley navigates through the South Glens Falls defense during the Section 2 Class B championship game on Sunday at Glens Falls High School. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) Key moment Riley Rodecker got Burnt Hills on the board midway through the first quarter, and the Spartans kept the momentum the rest of the way. The top-seeded Spartans, who received a bye into the title game, scored two goals in the first quarter and two in the second, to take a 4-0 lead into the half against the second-seeded Bulldogs. They added another goal in the third and fourth quarters for a 6-1 victory. "We always tell them, ‘Next game,'" said Burnt Hills coach Kelly Vrooman. "I know we have this game (under control), but we have to look ahead to the next game, to stick to the details and (uphold) the standard we have here." Star of the game A mix of Burnt Hills' senior leaders and youngsters made an impact on the scoreboard on Sunday. While Kogut had two goals and an assist and Lansley had two assists, freshman forward Carah DiCaprio had the standout performance with three goals and an assist. Maeve McCarty punched in the lone goal for South Glens Falls in the third quarter, as she navigated her way down the field for an unassisted score. item.title: Rays decline options on Martinez & Mullins
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 23: Nick Martinez #28 of the Tampa Bay Rays throws a pitch during the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game one of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field on October 23, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Rays have officially parted ways with two veteran players that were integral to the team’s run to the World Series this past season. On Friday, October 30th, the Rays announced that they had declined the mutual options for the 2027 season with RHP Nick Martinez and OF Cedric Mullins. The Rays signed Martinez just prior to Spring Training to a one year, $9M contract with a $20M mutual option for the 2027 season; the Rays paid Martinez a $4M buyout after declining that option. The signing could not have worked out any better for Tampa Bay and Martinez as the veteran hurler delivered one of his best seasons and was named an All-Star for the first time in his career. Overall the 36 year old compiled a 3.10 ERA | 3.96 FIP with a 15.1 K% and league leading 3.6 BB% over a career high, 180 IP. Off the field, Martinez’s leadership within the clubhouse was invaluable as he helped guide a young Rays team to their first postseasom berth since 2023. When the Rays reached the World Series for the third time in franchise history, Nick Martinez received the honor of starting Game One against the Milwaukee Brewers. Early last offseason, the Rays signed the veteran Cedric Mullins to a one year, $7M deal with a $10M mutual option for the 2027 season. The Rays have declined that option and instead paid Mullins a $500K buyout. Mullins wasn’t able to recapture the magic that had made him one of the top players in baseball while with the Baltimore Orioles several years ago. The now 32 year old Mullins had one of the worst offensive seasons in baseball in 2026 and also posted the lowest OBP% among qualifying players in a single-season for the Rays. Overall Mullins hit .205/.284/.344 with 15 HR and 21 SB, registering a 76 wRC+ (4th lowest of 135 players). Mullins did accrue 1.1 fWAR despite his lowly offensive production thanks to plus defense in center field, producing 11 Outs Above Average, which ranked 4th among 54 qualifying outfielders. With the departures of Mullins and Martinez, the Rays will likely be on the hunt for new veteran additions to fill their respective roles on the team.

item.title: Token thieves costing companies $100K+ per day in illicit LLM charges
item.description: Victim organizations are losing millions of dollars in token charges as criminals hijack their corporate LLM access to steal expensive computing resources and AI services. These fraudulent charges from resource consumption can exceed $100,000 a day, according to a Monday report by Google's Mandiant incident responders, who saw cumulative charges at some organizations hit $1 million before the victim companies revoked intruders' access. "Whenever possible, threat actors want to use this technology to gain a scale advantage over defenders. They achieve that with agentic tools and by stealing tokens from unwitting third parties,” John Hultquist, chief analyst at Google Threat Intelligence Group, told The Register . “Locking down these resources will not only protect organizations from runaway costs, but also protect the broader community from a deluge of cheap, autonomous attacks.” This tactic of hijacking access to LLMs is called LLMJacking , and it’s been increasing steadily over the past two years. In one extreme case, documented in an August report from CrowdStrike, a token thief sent about 200,000 API requests in just two minutes. In one case detailed in the report, a group Google tracks as UNC6993 illicitly gained access to LLM API keys, then generated additional keys and enabled services within the victim’s cloud projects, racking up $100,000 in charges. The threat intel biz also documented a different token thief subscribing victim accounts to Pay-As-You-Go agreements to access advanced models on the victim company’s dime. The crook selected premium foundation models, launched high-volume inference streams, and used a “burn and rotate strategy” to bypass rate limits by creating and deleting short-lived service accounts while auditing the billing interface to monitor financial impact. In yet another incident, an intruder executed more than 500,000 LLM API calls in less than eight hours using stolen third-party API keys to power a token routing service called Jet Night, according to a Monday report from Google. “Given Jet Night’s per-token costs to users are so far below typical market rates GTIG believes the service relies on stolen keys to operate profitably,” the report says. “For example, Jet Night offers an unlimited token plan for approximately $60 USD per month with alleged access to frontier models, a consumer service level that would typically run between $100 and $250 per month.” Jet Night has also admitted to multiple outages on its public Telegram channel, which the Google threat hunters note is “likely due to stolen keys being revoked as victims discover their respective compromises.” Specialized LLMjacking roles As more criminals join the LLMJacking ecosystem, Google says it has documented a division of labor between the criminals that establish initial access to compromised cloud and AI services, and those that manage downstream monetization infrastructure, called “LLM Mixers.” In one case that Mandiant responded to in mid-2026,

item.title: Miner dies in pit collapse in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — A 35-year-old miner, identified as Ibrahim Jabir, has died following the collapse of a mining pit at Asaradan village in Jos East Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 12:10 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, 2026, trapping the miner in the collapsed pit. A resident of Jos East, Peter Ajik, who confirmed the incident to newsmen in Jos on Monday, said Jabir died at the scene. “The victim, Ibrahim Jabir, died in the incident. The incident happened around 12:10 a.m. when the mining pit collapsed,” Ajik said. He described the incident as another reminder of the dangers associated with mining activities, particularly where adequate safety measures are not observed. Ajik urged miners to take safety precautions seriously and called on relevant authorities to intensify monitoring of mining activities in the area. He also said security operatives responded to a distress call following the collapse. “We are appealing to the relevant authorities to intensify monitoring of mining activities in the area and ensure that safety measures are strictly observed to prevent further loss of lives,” he said. Efforts to reach security operatives for further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Miner dies in pit collapse in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Democrats, Trump hold final rallies before midterm elections
item.description: Donald Trump and his Republican Party will make last-gasp pitches to US midterm voters Monday to hold back a predicted Democrat wave that could sweep Congress and impose tight political constraints on the president for the first time in two years. For his closing arguments, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president’s controversial drive to redevelop the US capital. “We’re going to win,” he said on Sunday. Democrats, meanwhile, prepared a round of final rallies — including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas — which will cap a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness. Polls are largely in their favor, showing that Democrats are poised to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate. Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues. The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into a lame-duck period, with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran, and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington. But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats are wary about predictions of victory. “Nauseously optimistic,” Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood. – Scorched earth – Democrats are also facing late internal divisions, with left-wing candidates clashing at times with the party’s establishment. In a startling display of infighting on Sunday, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens in Michigan endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed in her state’s key Senate race. Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, struggled to explain her decision in an interview with CNN. Trump’s Republicans have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding El-Sayed, who is Muslim, as a terrorist. Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are “extreme and dangerous radicals” who will “steal your wealth” and let in migrants to “ransack, rape and plunder.” But polls show Americans souring on Trump’s wrecking-ball act. While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air. Only a third of the Senate’s 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favorable to Democrats. To win the upper chamber, Democrats must flip seats in states the president carried by double digits two years before. This has only happened five times in midterm elections since 1990. item.title: Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,300 people – Africa CDC
item.description: Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency. In mid-May, the DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak, a deadly disease transmitted through contact with bodily fluids that causes haemorrhagic fever and has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years. According to data shared with AFP by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) on Monday, the outbreak, which has spread to other countries on the continent, has killed 5,376 people — 5,372 in the DRC and two each in Kenya and Uganda. A total of 10,444 cases have been confirmed, with a fatality rate of more than 50 percent. The virus has crossed borders several times in recent months. Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 cases, almost all involving people who had travelled from the DRC, before being declared Ebola-free in August. In October, Kenya recorded nine infections, marking the first time the country had reported an Ebola case. That same month, Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, reported an Ebola case involving a 42-year-old Swiss woman whose husband works at the Swiss embassy in Abuja. The couple had travelled to Uganda before returning to Nigeria. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which no approved vaccine or treatment is currently available. In recent weeks, clinical trials have begun with the Ervebo vaccine, which has proved effective against the more common Zaire strain of the virus. The President described the honour as a historic and deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. “I want to say a big thank you for the faith and recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in green, white and green, which reminds us of our Nigerian identity. “I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the Holy Land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and of the country. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us, but we will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I am grateful forever. I thank the King and the Crown Prince. “It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history,” the President said. President Tinubu said he asked Allah for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians, and expressed confidence that his prayers have been answered. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue serving the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. item.title: Using 1963 Fire Act to fight 2026 fires unacceptable, FG declares
item.description: .Unveils vision of new fire and rescue service .Cuts response time to 15 minutes, 119 lives saved By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has said it makes no sense to continue to rely on a fire law enacted in 1963 to tackle fire emergencies in 2026, as it prepares to send a new Federal Fire and Rescue Service Act to President Bola Tinubu soon for assent. Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said this on Monday in Abuja at the opening ceremony and stakeholders’ conference of the 2026 National Fire Safety Week. “You cannot have a Federal Fire Service Act of 1963, and you think it would be 2026-compliant. It doesn’t make sense” the minister said. He said the old law denies firefighters the powers they need to do their work. “If the law does not give you the power to do something, no matter how good that action is, once you do it, it becomes illegal. There is no right way of doing something that is legally wrong,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said the review of the Act had been completed and the new bill should be laid before the President in a matter of days. He said it was the first time in 63 years that any government had taken up the task. The minister said the new law would open the sector to private sector intervention and move the service beyond firefighting. “When it comes to hazards, fire is only one of the hazards. Even flood, water can be hazardous,” he said. He said he wanted a Federal Fire Service that responds to medical emergencies, floods, chemical spills, toxic materials, bomb attacks and earthquakes. He added that fire suppression was only one of about twenty responsibilities of fire services elsewhere. “I want to see a Federal Fire Service whose specialisation is rescue operations,” he said. Tunji-Ojo also called for stronger fire inspection and code enforcement, with volunteer fire marshals in every district and town. He said the service should work with education authorities to make rescue skills part of school curricula. “If anything happens, maybe somebody faints, what percentage of Nigerians can even do a simple resuscitation process?” he asked. The minister said the service should also investigate emergencies beyond fire incidents, and should chair a council of fire and rescue services to coordinate policy across the country. On performance, the minister said the average response time to fire incidents was between 32 and 35 minutes when the administration came into office. He said it now stands at 15 minutes, 22 seconds. He said that as of August, 119 lives were saved with no life lost to fire in 36 incidents nationwide. “There is a lot he’s working under the old law, so there’s a limit to how well he can do this,” Tunji-Ojo said of the Controller-General of the Federal Fire Service, Olumode Samuel Adeyemi. The minister said the National Fire Academy was 85 per cent complete and would be running by the end of the year, with commissioning expected in December. He described it as “one of the best academies in the world”. E

item.title: 2027: Give Tinubu, Otu another term, Shettima tells Cross River
item.description: …says authority belongs to the people …Bakassi Deep seaport will be one Nigeria’s maritime gateway By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR Nigeria’s vice president, Senator Kashim Shettima, on Monday, held out the promise of a deep seaport in Bakassi and the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway to Cross River voters, asking them to renew the mandate of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027. Representing the President at the APC Presidential Campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Shettima brought the President’s greetings and thanked the people for standing by the administration. “Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said. He described the relationship with the people of Cross River and Nogeria at large as “an alliance of prosperity, an alliance of opportunity”. He said the APC was seeking votes for Tinubu, Governor Otu, and candidates for the National Assembly and the State House of Assembly. “We are asking because authority belongs to the people. Those entrusted with authority must return with an account of their stewardship.” Turning to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, he said the project would “connect coastal communities” and “ease the movement of goods and people.” He added that it would expand tourism, attract investors and create thousands of direct and indirect jobs. On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, he said the project had received federal government approval. “When completed, it will become an international maritime gateway. It will attract shipping companies. It will generate employment,” he said. He said the two projects were part of a plan to make Cross River a major beneficiary of the government’s maritime economy agenda. The vice president also spoke about education, saying the government’s student financing intervention would drive human capital development in the state. He said it would give relief to parents and widen access to higher education so that no parent would be forced to abandon a child’s schooling for lack of funds. Shettima praised the party faithful at the rally, saying they were “chosen by you, endorsed by you.” He asked them to vote for the APC “from top to bottom” in the 2027 elections. “You, the people, are the purpose and authority of you,” he declared. item.title: 2027: Critics of Rainbow Coalition incapable of uniting their own families – Wike
item.description: …Tells FCT residents, ‘election day is not for market or fishing’ By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said politicians who deny the existence of the Rainbow Coalition lack the capacity to unite even their own families and communities. Wike spoke on Monday in Abuja at the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civic Centre and an interactive session with stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress APC and the Peoples Democratic Party PDP in Gwagwalada Area Council. The minister said the coalition, which brings together political stakeholders from both parties, was formed in the interest of unity, cooperation and development in the FCT. “Some greedy and selfish politicians do not understand what we call unity. They have no capacity to hold their space, they have no capacity to even hold their families, and they have no capacity to hold their communities. So they can open their mouths and say there is no Rainbow Coalition,” he said. Wike challenged critics of the alliance to explain why political leaders who once disagreed could not come together to pursue common interests. He described the development in Gwagwalada as a departure from the politics of confrontation, insisting that the FCT needed cooperation rather than needless political hostility. Commending political leaders in the area for setting aside their differences, he said their decision showed that the collective interest of the people outweighed individual political ambition. Wike also urged residents not to repeat what he described as the mistake of the 2023 general elections and called for credible representation at the National Assembly. The minister canvassed support for a former senator, Philip Aduda, and other candidates endorsed by the coalition, saying political representatives must be accessible and familiar with their constituents. Wike also declared support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and urged residents to turn their endorsements into votes in 2027. “On the day of the election, it will not be a day for market or fishing. It is the day all of us have decided to come together and demonstrate our strength through our votes. Go to the polling units, districts and communities and mobilise the people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, described the gathering as historic, saying Wike’s intervention had brought together leaders who previously operated on opposing sides. The FCT PDP Chairman, Alhaji Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, praised Wike for his development interventions, particularly the revival of a project abandoned for 16 years in Gwagwalada. The Aguma of Gwagwalada, Alhaji Muhammadu Magaji, also commended Wike’s contributions to the development of the territory. He said the revival of the abandoned project underscored the importance of continuity in governance. item.title: 2027: Obi couldn’t fix Anambra; Atiku will return to Dubai after election — Oshiomhole
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Senator Adams Oshiomhole has criticised former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, questioning their capacity to lead Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Oshiomhole said Obi failed to address Anambra State’s challenges during his eight years as governor, while predicting that Atiku would return to Dubai after losing the presidential election. The former Edo State governor made the remarks during an All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally in Cross River State, where he urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Questioning Obi’s promise to govern Nigeria for only four years, Oshiomhole said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDCa) had not demonstrated the capacity to deliver within that period. “If Peter Obi could not fix Anambra State in eight years, how can he look you korokoro in the eye and say he will do it in four years?” he asked. He also took a swipe at Atiku, accusing the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of spending much of his time outside the country and returning to Nigeria during election periods. “Atiku, who lives in Dubai, only comes home at the eve of every election. When he loses this one, as he will lose, in January or by February, Atiku will be back in Dubai,” he said. Oshiomhole, however, used the campaign to highlight what he described as the achievements of the Tinubu administration, particularly in Cross River State. He said the state’s recognition as an oil-producing state following the resolution of its non-littoral status would increase revenue accruing to the state and improve its economic prospects. On education, the senator said the Federal Government’s student loan scheme had provided opportunities for young people whose parents could not afford their school fees. He described Tinubu as a leader who prioritises access to education, arguing that students should not be denied opportunities because of their parents’ financial circumstances. Oshiomhole also pointed to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road project, saying its completion would bring economic opportunities and development to Cross River State. The senator also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic policies, particularly the abolition of multiple exchange rates. He argued that the previous system created different exchange rates for people based on their connections, adding that the current arrangement had established a uniform exchange rate across the country. According to Oshiomhole, implementing the policies required courage and visionary leadership. He urged Cross River residents to reject the opposition parties, insisting that the APC had established a strong political presence in the state. “Today, tomorrow, and forever, I believe APC has come to stay in Cross River, and together we will advance the growth and development of Nigeria,” he said. item.title: SUSE to cut one in ten employees because of... AI
item.description: One in ten employees at SUSE are facing the chop due to "automation and AI," according to a memo dispatched by management at the privately owned open source software biz. In an email to the 1,900 strong workforce on Monday - seen by The Register - CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen, the former Red Hat exec who joined SUSE in March 2023, confirmed the "difficult news." "We are announcing a reduction of SUSE’s global workforce of approximately 10 percent," he said. "These decisions are painful for our people, our culture, and our open source community, but they are necessary for us to adapt and build a sustainable, resilient SUSE for the long term." Van Leeuwen says the business, bought by Swedish private equity provider EQT, decided to cut jobs after scrutinizing its "future strategy, required capabilities, and team structures." The rest of the organization will get a look at the fiscal year 2027 strategy on November 16. He said in the message to staff: "What is clear is that automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate. AI capabilities are advancing exponentially, forcing us to radically reimagine our work. We have seen this trend already both inside our sector and in the wider economy. This means that the organizational design and cost base that SUSE is built on today will not carry us forward successfully. "We are adapting. Across SUSE, modern tooling is already changing our daily workflows, enabling teams to move faster with less operational overhead and flatter reporting lines. The requirement for some existing roles has greatly diminished. Other roles will evolve over the next few years. This means we are accelerating investments in high priority areas, and deprioritizing others. These are hard, painful decisions to make, but necessary for our future." As The Reg reported in 2025, SUSE doubled down on AI . The specific roles at risk of redundancy were not outlined but SUSE claims it has considered where the people in those positions are "able to evolve, what they can stop doing, what they need to do more of - and decisions have been made on that basis." Staff caught up in the redundancies will be informed by November 4, employee representatives nominated the following day, and one to one meetings will begin at the start of next week. Van Leeuwen says in the internal memo that the job cuts are a "reflection of shifting organizational needs, not your talent or commitment. You have tackled hard infrastructure and open source challenges that power critical enterprise systems around the world. "Any organization will be fortunate to have your expertise." Back in September, we reported that the company was asking old hands if they would take "voluntary separation ." It seems not enough people chose to walk through the door, so instead, they're getting thrown through it instead. SUSE "geckos" in the Czech Republic may be glad they joined a trade union . Back in 2018, EQT bought SUSE from Microfocus for $2.5 billion. EQT floate

item.title: 2027: Accord Party challenges suit seeking to disqualify all its candidates
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Accord Party (AP) has approached the Federal High Court in Abuja for the dismissal of a suit seeking to disqualify all its candidates for the 2027 general elections. The party, in a preliminary objection filed through a team of lawyers led by a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Mr. Musibau Adetunbi, maintained that the court lacks the jurisdiction to entertain the legal action filed by its National Secretary, Mr. Adebukola Ajaja. It argued that the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CV/2524/2026, lacked competence as it was filed outside the 14-day period allowed by law. Insisting that the action had become statute-barred, the party further contended that the issue bordered on the nomination of candidates, which it said falls within the domestic affairs of a political party and is non-justiciable. Moreover, while querying the locus standi (legal right) of the plaintiff to file the action, Accord Party noted that he is not an aspirant in the primary election it conducted on May 29. It also faulted the competence of the suit on the ground that proper parties were not included. The Accord Party argued that while the plaintiff wants the court to nullify the nomination of its candidates, none of the candidates who would be affected by the outcome of the suit were made parties, to afford them the opportunity of being heard. The party further described the suit as “premature”, arguing that the plaintiff failed to give the required 21 days’ pre-action notice. It told the court that its primary was conducted in accordance with all relevant laws and guidelines, adding that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has since recognised its outcome and the list of candidates duly submitted to the electoral umpire in the prescribed format. It further argued that, contrary to the plaintiff’s contention, the National Chairman and the National Organising Secretary could validly sign and submit candidates’ lists and forms to INEC where the National Secretary is unavailable, in line with Article 18 of the party’s constitution and Regulations 25(3) and 28(2) of INEC’s Guidelines. Accord Party added: “INEC Regulations and Guidelines for Political Parties did not in any way specify that the plaintiff herein must sign the forwarding letter, neither did the Constitution of the second defendant require her (the plaintiff) to sign. “The National Executives of the party expressly authorized the fourth defendant to co-sign with the 3rd Defendant. No wrong has been done.” Relying on the Supreme Court’s decision in Jegede v. INEC, Accord Party argued that even if only its National Chairman had signed, “the plaintiff’s case is still bound to fail because the signature of the National Chairman suffices on the authority of Jegede v. INEC.” In a counter-affidavit deposed to by its National Chairman, Maxwell Mgbudem, the party told the court that, contrary to the plaintiff’s claim that her responsibilities were usurped by the National Organising Sec

item.title: Heading into the midterms, 'no US president in recent times has been as unpopular as Donald Trump'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections. Far from assuming that Trump's formidable campaigning instincts can once again mobilize Republican voters, Johnson questions whether the president's political influence has become a liability for the very party he once transformed. He points to a potentially significant realignment within the American electorate. Economic grievances, rising living costs, trade disputes and disillusionment with the war in Iran appear, in Johnson's reading, to be weakening important elements of the coalition that sustained Trump's return to power. Particularly consequential is the possibility that Latino voters, agricultural communities and sections of the MAGA electorate may be reconsidering their political loyalties or withdrawing from electoral participation altogether.

item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Two persons have been killed while five others sustained injuries in separate attacks on Toul and Halle communities in Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State. The attacks reportedly occurred at about 9pm on Sunday, November 1, 2026, when gunmen opened fire on residents in the two communities. A Mangu resident, Gabriel Titus, who confirmed the incidents to newsmen, said one person was killed and four others injured in the attack on Toul community. Titus said: “The gunmen came into the community and opened fire on the people. “Another person was killed in Halle, while one other person sustained injuries during the attack.” He lamented that the attacks occurred despite a curfew imposed by the state government to prevent further violence in the area. “There is a curfew in place, but the gunmen still came and carried out the attack,” he said. Titus appealed to security operatives to intensify surveillance and track down those responsible for the attacks. He also called for urgent measures to protect residents of the affected communities, saying the recurring violence had heightened concerns among residents. item.title: Reps propose 20% cap on trust investments
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has proposed a 20 per cent investment limit on exposure to a single issuer as part of efforts to strengthen the management of trust funds and protect beneficiaries against financial losses. The proposal is contained in the Trustee Investment Bill, 2026 (HB 2762), which seeks to repeal and re-enact the existing Trustee Investments Act of 1957, expand permissible investment opportunities and introduce safeguards against excessive investment risks. Chairman of the House Committee on Capital Market and Institutions, Solomon Bob, disclosed this on Monday at a public hearing on the bill at the National Assembly, Abuja. Bob described the proposed diversification requirement as a critical measure to prevent excessive concentration of trust assets in one investment. He said the existing law was enacted when Nigeria’s financial system was considerably less developed and investment opportunities were limited. According to him, the country’s financial landscape has changed significantly, with the capital market now valued at over N80 trillion, pension assets exceeding N30 trillion and emerging investment opportunities including Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), infrastructure funds and green bonds. “Today, we have a sophisticated capital market worth over N80 trillion, pension assets over N30 trillion, and new asset classes from REITs to Infrastructure Funds to Green Bonds. The world has moved. Our law has not. This hearing is to correct that,” he said. Bob said the proposed legislation was designed to align the legal framework governing trust investments with contemporary financial realities while ensuring that trustees operated within clearly defined investment and accountability standards. Under Clause 3 of the bill, the investment options available to trustees would be expanded to include corporate bonds, equities, collective investment schemes, including Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) and REITs, infrastructure funds, real property, foreign investments through licensed custodians, private equity, regulated virtual assets and environmental, social and governance (ESG)-compliant bonds. He said the expanded investment options would allow trustees to diversify portfolios and potentially improve returns for beneficiaries. However, Bob explained that the proposed 20 per cent limit on investment in a single issuer under Clause 4 was intended to minimise concentration risk and prevent trust portfolios from being excessively exposed to the financial difficulties of one institution. The bill also seeks to strengthen trustees’ fiduciary obligations through Clause 5 by expressly incorporating the principles of loyalty, prudence, care and impartiality. Under the proposed provision, trustees would be required to exercise the level of prudence expected of individuals managing their own financial affairs, while prioritising the interests of beneficiaries. item.title: Cyberattacks disrupt supermarket fridges across five European countries
item.description: Supermarkets in at least five European countries have been hit by a cyberattack that disrupted refrigeration systems, causing temperatures in some fridges and freezers to rise sharply. The affected countries include Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Luxembourg and Sweden, with several retailers confirming on Monday that their systems had been targeted by hackers. The incident comes about three weeks after a similar cyberattack affected refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets across France, forcing retailers to dispose of spoiled food and raising concerns about food security. No individual or group has claimed responsibility for either attack. In Belgium, Carrefour reported disruptions in about 15 of its 700 stores. The company’s spokesman, Mich Vergauwen, confirmed that the incident was a cyberattack. An Ikea Belgium spokeswoman also said its store in Mons, southwestern Belgium, was affected, with freezer temperatures rising suddenly in the early hours of Monday. Other affected retailers included Delhaize, Colruyt and Intermarche. Delhaize also reported refrigeration problems in four of its stores in Luxembourg. Belgian industrial refrigeration company Sabcobel said it had begun securing its installations following the October 12 attack in France. However, about 10 per cent of the systems had yet to be fixed, including some in stores affected by Monday’s incident. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Stephan Moelans, told AFP that the impact would have been significantly worse if the security operation had not started earlier. In Sweden, supermarket chain Coop confirmed that six of its approximately 800 stores were affected by a cyber incident on Monday. Its spokesman, Carlos Cancino, said the problem had been resolved and that refrigeration systems were operating normally. He added that the affected stores were connected to a 4G mobile network rather than the updated 5G system, making them more exposed to cyberattacks. The company, however, said it did not know who was responsible. Another Swedish retailer, Ica, reported refrigeration problems in a limited number of stores but said it could not confirm whether they resulted from a cyberattack. Ica spokeswoman Helena Johansson said the affected stores were connected to an external refrigeration control system supplied by Danish manufacturer Danfoss, the same company whose equipment was reportedly involved in the October 12 incident in France. Danfoss had yet to respond to AFP’s request for comment. In Finland, irregular temperatures were detected in some smaller grocery stores operated by the Kesko group. The company’s head of corporate security, Petri Kayhko, said investigations were ongoing and that interference through the network had not been ruled out. Roni Kokkola, an information security specialist at Finland’s National Cyber Security Centre, also said a cyberattack could not be excluded. He noted that similar incidents had occurred elsewhere in Europe in recent months, adding that th

item.title: Six mourners abducted in Benue, N15m ransom demanded
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Six persons, including a man conveying his deceased wife’s corpse from Kano State to Okpoga, headquarters of Okpokwu Local Government Area of Benue State, for burial, have been abducted along Adoka Road in Otukpo Local Government Area. The abductors have reportedly demanded N15 million ransom for the release of the victims. The victims, comprising the bereaved husband and five other mourners accompanying him, were reportedly kidnapped at about 8pm on Friday, while the woman’s corpse was abandoned in their vehicle. A community member, Meddy Olotu, who raised the alarm over the incident, said the victims had remained in captivity since Friday, while efforts to secure their release had yet to yield results as of Monday. According to him, the victims were returning from Kano, where the woman died, and heading to Okpoga for her burial when they were intercepted along Adoka Road. Olotu said: “The man, who is based in Kano, lost his wife, and they were bringing her corpse back home to Okpoga in Okpokwu LGA of Benue State for burial. “They left Kano, and you can imagine the journey from Kano to Benue State. It is a long journey. They got to Adoka at about 8pm. That was the last time the family members could reach them. “That same Friday, around Adoka Road, they were said to have been kidnapped and whisked into the bush, while the corpse of his late wife was left in the vehicle. There were about six of them. “From that Friday till today, Monday, they have not been released. As I speak to you, we learnt the abductors are demanding N15 million ransom.” Describing the incident as particularly distressing, Olotu said the abduction had compounded the grief of the family, which was already mourning the loss of the woman. “For somebody who lost his wife, they kidnapped him and his five friends and left the wife’s corpse on the road. That is terrible,” he said. He said personnel of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) reportedly found the corpse the following morning and took it to the police station at Adoka, from where it was deposited in a mortuary pending the release of the abducted persons. Olotu added that the abductors had maintained contact with the victims’ family, with one of the relatives reportedly able to communicate with them because he understood the language they spoke. “Last night, I spoke with one of the family members who said the people have been calling. Luckily, he understands Hausa, so he is able to communicate with them,” he said. He said the six victims were still being held in the bush as of Monday, while the woman’s corpse remained in a mortuary in Adoka. Olotu appealed to relevant authorities to intensify efforts to rescue the victims, expressing concern that the family might struggle to raise the ransom demanded. Confirming the incident, Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Council, Maxwell Ogiri, said the abduction occurred along Adoka Road. item.title: A rainbow of ancient rocks on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 2, 2026
item.description: null In this image, we can see a colorful view of an ancient, rocky Martian hill. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona) This rainbow-hued rocky plain looks like the landscape of an alien world. And, it turns out, it is. What is it? In this image, we can see an ancient, rocky hill on Mars . In the Red Planet's Southern Highlands, this alien terrain is chock-full of minerals, which we can see clearly defined in this color-enhanced view of the region. This image was snapped by the HiRISE camera aboard NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter ( MRO ), which has been studying the planet's surface, atmosphere and climate since arriving in Martian orbit in March 2006. But this isn't exactly what the surface of the planet would look like through our eyes; the image is color-enhanced. Why would scientists take a natural-color image and turn it rainbow? Doing so enhances the slight color differences in these rocks, allowing researchers to pick out the different minerals. Why is it incredible? As pointed to above, enhancing colors in scientific images can be an incredibly useful tool for exploration. For instance, in this image, the blue- and green-toned rocks could be full of minerals like pyroxenes and olivine, according to scientists analyzing the image. And they think that the yellow, orange and red patches may contain minerals formed by past interactions with liquid water. By exploring the mineral content of rocks like this, researchers can peel back the layers of history within the Martian bedrock. The discovery of certain minerals, for example, can show that water flowed on Mars long ago, pointing to potentially habitable conditions . So, as we can see, this striking rainbow image isn't just a beautiful landscape; it's also hiding serious clues to Mars' history.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 2, 2000: Expedition 1 Arrives at the International Space Station
item.description: null On Nov. 2, 2000, the International Space Station welcomed its first long-term residents: NASA astronaut Bill Shepherd and two Russian cosmonauts, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev. The mission was called Expedition 1. Before this expedition, NASA had launched five, one-week-long Space Shuttle missions to help build the space station and bring up supplies. But this time, the crew would be staying for four and a half months, and they weren't taking the shuttle. Instead, they took a Russian Soyuz spacecraft , and this was the first Soyuz to ever dock at the space station. During their stay at the space station, they unpacked supplies and installed new equipment, including the first solar arrays. They left on the space shuttle Discovery, which brought up the Expedition 2 crew that would take their place. Expedition 1 crewmates Bill Shepherd, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev pose with a model of the space station as it appeared in 2000. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As of today, there has been a continuous astronaut presence in space aboard the International Space Station for 26 years. For all of these years, not a day has gone by without someone living in space, orbiting our planet from aboard the space station. While the ISS was not the first space station, it has been the longest-running space statin by far. This first crew were pioneers, showing how humans could actually live and work aboard this station. This exploratory mission proved that the station could successfully support astronaut crews. Since this mission 26 years ago, there have been literally hundreds of astronauts from around the world who have flown to and lived aboard the ISS. While NASA has stated that the station might be decommissioned in the coming years, these accomplishments will remain forever in spaceflight history. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Nigerian teenager convicted for defrauding American man of $800
item.description: The Federal High Court sitting in Ikoyi, Lagos, has convicted and sentenced an 18-year-old man, Hassan Usman Olamilekan, for money laundering involving $800 obtained through a lottery scam. Justice Dipeolu delivered the judgment on October 30, 2026, following Olamilekan’s arraignment by the Lagos Zonal Directorate 1 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Olamilekan was arraigned on a one-count charge of money laundering, contrary to Section 18(2)(a) and punishable under Section 18(3) of the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. The defendant pleaded guilty to the charge, after which an EFCC operative, Ebuka Abanga, reviewed the facts of the case before the court found him guilty. Justice Dipeolu sentenced him to a fine of N200,000 and ordered him to pay N1 million in restitution to the Federal Government. The court further ordered that he remains in the correctional centre pending payment of the fine and restitution. It also ordered the forfeiture of an iPhone 11 Pro and a Poco C71 mobile phone recovered in connection with the offence. According to the EFCC, investigations revealed that Olamilekan, who claimed to be from the Republic of Benin but was born in Nigeria, operated several social media platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Zangi and iMessage, which he allegedly used for internet fraud. The commission said he met his victim, an American citizen identified as Gary Brewer, through the Zangi application, where he impersonated a white American woman named Julie Leach. Olamilekan reportedly told Brewer that he had won a $250 million lottery prize but needed money to activate the winnings before he could claim the funds. He subsequently persuaded the victim to send him gift cards through the messaging platform. The EFCC said the defendant admitted selling the gift cards through the Cardsonic application, converting the proceeds into naira and transferring the money to his grandmother’s OPay account. He also confessed to benefiting $800 from the fraudulent scheme. Olamilekan was among 21 suspected internet fraudsters arrested by EFCC operatives during a sting operation at Applewood Estate, Orchid Road, Lekki, Lagos State, on October 26, 2026. item.title: Reps move to reform 69-year-old Trustee Investment Act
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has begun moves to reform Nigeria’s 69-year-old Trustee Investments Act, while seeking a coordinated regulatory framework to tackle fraud, fragmented property records and weak consumer protection in the real estate sector. Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, said the proposed reforms were aimed at modernising the country’s legal framework to reflect changing financial and investment realities, while protecting the interests of beneficiaries and investors. Abbas, represented by a member of the House representing Lafia/Obi Federal Constituency, Nasarawa State, Dahiru Abubakar Sarki, spoke on Monday at a public hearing on the Trustee Investment Act (Repeal and Enactment) Bill, 2026, at the National Assembly, Abuja. The bill, sponsored by Solomon Bob, seeks to repeal and replace the existing Trustee Investments Act of 1957, which Abbas described as outdated in the face of developments in Nigeria’s capital market and emerging investment opportunities. He said the existing law was enacted in a substantially different economic and financial environment, noting that the investment landscape had changed considerably over the past seven decades. According to him, capital markets have expanded, financial instruments have become more sophisticated, and new opportunities for investment and wealth creation have emerged, making legislative reform necessary. “The challenge is to strike the right balance between preserving trust assets and enabling reasonable returns on investment. “An excessively restrictive framework may deny beneficiaries legitimate opportunities for growth, while an inadequately regulated one may expose their assets to imprudent decisions and avoidable risks,” he said. Abbas stressed that expanded investment opportunities under the proposed legislation must be accompanied by strong safeguards, clear fiduciary responsibilities, effective risk management and appropriate regulatory oversight. He said trustees must be guided by prudence, integrity and transparency, adding that assets held in trust must be managed in the interests of beneficiaries rather than for the personal advantage of trustees. The Speaker said a credible framework for managing trust investments could contribute to deeper capital markets and more effective mobilisation of domestic resources to support infrastructure development and economic growth. He urged stakeholders to pay particular attention to investment categories, diversification requirements, fiduciary obligations, professional delegation and regulatory oversight in considering the bill. Seeks coordinated real estate regulation In a related development, Abbas has called for a coordinated national real estate regulatory system to tackle property fraud, eliminate institutional overlaps and strengthen investor confidence in Nigeria’s housing market. He made the call in a keynote address at a stakeholders’ conference on the proposed National Real Estate Regulator

item.title: Binance Reopens Withdrawals as Hack Recovery Enters Second Week
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Reopens Withdrawals as Hack Recovery Enters Second Week Binance restarted customer withdrawals on Sunday, four days after hackers drained roughly $6.3 billion from its hot wallets in the largest crypto theft on record. The exchange reopened in stages over the weekend, starting with bitcoin and expanding to 15 networks. The move marked the first real test of whether the platform could absorb a loss of that size without freezing its customers out for longer. The recovery push began Saturday. In its third recovery update, Binance said it had replenished 90% of the impacted amount with company funds. The exchange drew on part of its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury to buy replacement tokens. The futures fund contribution drew particular attention, since Binance described the remaining balance as a regulatory requirement. Binance also published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot dated October 31, giving users a baseline to check their balances against. Sunday’s reopening began at 06:00 UTC with BTC. Binance then added ETH, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, XRP, Dogecoin, Tron, Polygon, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Zcash, TON and Sui. Between 06:00 and 15:30 UTC, the exchange processed about $4.65 billion in withdrawals against roughly $1.01 billion in deposits. That produced a net outflow near $3.64 billion, equal to about 2.1% of the $171 billion in assets Binance reported in its late-October proof of reserves. Deposits stayed open throughout the rollout, and the exchange said temporary delays were possible during the initial surge in volume. Binance said its Sunday update raised coverage to 95% of the impacted amount. The remaining 5% sits in less liquid tokens outside the top ten assets on its proof-of-reserves list. Sourcing those tokens at the required scale takes more time, and the exchange said it is working with industry partners and over-the-counter desks to complete the purchases. Binance has committed to covering the full amount, and it has repeated that users will not bear the financial impact of the theft. On Monday, Binance said the full zero-knowledge proof for the October 31 snapshot is complete. Users holding BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD or ZEC can run the exchange’s verifier to confirm their balances are backed at least 1:1. The verifier is open source, and the exchange has pointed users to a step-by-step guide. The exchange plans another snapshot covering more tokens on November 4, with a proof expected to take 40 to 50 hours to generate. A further withdrawal phase is scheduled for Tuesday, and the exchange said it would share details once the rollout is ready. Binance hack background On the law enforcement front, the FBI has attributed the attack to North Korea, and the U.S. Secret Service is working with Circle to trace and freeze funds. item.title: The world has a new plan to save nature, but it still needs the money
item.description: The world is set to miss its 2030 conservation goals as finance and action have fallen short, leaders recognized at a UN biodiversity summit in Armenia’s capital, where they agreed to step up efforts after a final overnight session. Representatives from almost 200 countries gathered in Yerevan over the past two weeks to review progress on a landmark agreement set four years ago to protect about a third of the world’s land and seas by 2030. The COP17 talks on biodiversity concluded on Saturday with a recognition that conservation efforts were so far too slow to realistically achieve the goals of the 2022 Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. item.title: Nuclear threats and street brawls: Russia, Ukraine report attacks on their emergency alert apps
item.description: Cyberattacks on both Russia’s and Ukraine’s emergency alert apps resulted in fake messages about missile and nuclear strikes broadcast to the public. Officials from both countries confirmed the attacks, which occurred at similar times, on Sunday evening. According to public statements and messages sent via social media, Ukraine’s alert app was hit first, with the country’s Air Force quick to dispel nuclear fears. "The Air Alert app has likely been compromised," it said via Telegram at around 2100 UTC. "There is no radiation threat! Stay calm, follow our messages on our channel!" At around 0030 UTC on Monday, Russia's Ministry of Emergency Situations confirmed the country’s app had also been abused, with fake messages sent to citizens' devices. "Attention! The Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations' mobile app has been subjected to a massive cyberattack, allowing attackers to send fake information to the public," it said, also via Telegram. "Work is currently underway to patch the vulnerability and restore normal operation." The ministry issued an update around 90 minutes later, saying the app was once again functioning normally, and pointing out that an attack on the app was not the same as a compromise of the state’s national alert system. "Citizens are alerted through primary channels: regional and municipal alert systems (sirens, loudspeakers), communication networks (SMS messaging), and television and radio broadcasts. The mobile app is merely an additional, supporting information service," it stated. Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Affairs also issued a public announcement reminding citizens about how to receive emergency warnings while its “Alarm!” app was down. These include enabling iOS and Android emergency alerts, state-controlled sirens, and other official sources, such as the official social media accounts of Ukraine's government. According to the messages sent to devices after the compromise of Ukraine's alert app, the fake warnings pertained to various threats, such as street fights in Kyiv, chemical attacks, and radiation hazards. Alerts about the threat of nuclear fallout from official government warning systems would normally lead to panic, however, one of the earliest messages sent to citizens was written in Russian and referenced the "Oreshnik" missile, which was an immediate signal that the message may not be genuine. Equivalent alerts sent to Russian citizens also warned of impending nuclear strikes "at all regions of Russia," referencing "P1-Sun," the name of a Ukrainian attack drone. Oleksander Merezhko, who chairs the Ukrainian parliament's foreign affairs committee and noted the suspicious Russian-language alert, told the BBC the attack was almost certainly part of Russia's cyber war . "It's a very unpleasant fact but it is part of cyber war and people in Ukraine understand that," he said. "It is possible and we are quite prepared for such possibilities." item.title: Microsoft's Canada timezone troubles leave admins fixing calendars, pretending they're in Bogota
item.description: Microsoft has discovered once again that few things strike fear into the heart of a software engineer quite like a government deciding to fiddle with the clocks. Parts of Canada stopped observing seasonal clock changes on November 1, leaving affected areas of British Columbia, Alberta, and Manitoba permanently on UTC-07:00, UTC-06:00 and UTC-05:00 respectively. Unfortunately, Microsoft's sprawling software empire hasn't entirely caught up. The company has confirmed problems across a chunk of its software estate, leaving some customers facing incorrect times, broken schedules and a collection of workarounds while Redmond catches up. Outlook users have been left with the most homework. Switching to the new Canadian time zones won't automatically update existing calendar entries, meaning that meetings scheduled after November 1 are potentially an hour out of whack. Microsoft advises users to change their Outlook calendar time zone, then update upcoming events and meetings to use it. For meetings involving other people, only the organizer can make the change. Recurring meetings come with an additional treat: changing the time zone resets any previously moved occurrences, which then have to be recreated. Anyone with a calendar full of recurring meetings may wish to put the kettle on first. Microsoft is working on an Exchange Online PowerShell cmdlet to remediate non-recurring meetings, but according to its guidance, that's not due until later this week. A fix for recurring meetings remains "in development," with an ETA yet to be confirmed. Things get stranger with Power Automate and Fabric, where Microsoft's temporary fix involves pretending you're somewhere else entirely. Depending on the product and province, that could mean Saskatchewan, Arizona or, for Manitobans, Bogota. Because apparently time zones weren't confusing enough already. SharePoint On-Prem customers, meanwhile, have to wait until November 10 for the correct time zones to arrive, while Power Pages users could see server-formatted dates appear an hour out until a service fix lands. Microsoft's current milestone for that is December 12. Admins dealing with the fallout aren't exactly delighted. One sysadmin on Reddit said Microsoft's guidance had been "terrible" and claimed to have written roughly 900 lines of PowerShell to change users' Outlook settings and manually adjust calendar events. Others described switching systems to Saskatchewan time while waiting for Microsoft's new zones to settle in. Microsoft published its guidance on October 26, less than a week before the change took effect, and was still adding affected products and workarounds four days later. Meanwhile, admins were urged to test calendars, recurring meetings, and schedules before the November 1 switch, leaving little time to find out what might break. item.title: Strategy (MSTR) Adds 811 Bitcoin, Strive (ASST) Follows Suit With 124 as Both Keep Stacking
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy (MSTR) Adds 811 Bitcoin, Strive (ASST) Follows Suit With 124 as Both Keep Stacking Strategy bought another 811 bitcoin last week. The Saylor-led firm spent about $65.5 million at an average of $80,846 per coin between October 26 and November 1, according to its 8-K filing on Monday. That brings total holdings to 849,327 BTC, bought for roughly $64.1 billion at an average of $75,451. The money didn’t come from new preferred stock this time. Strategy sold about 1.18 million shares of MSTR common stock for roughly $164 million, sent $65.5 million into bitcoin, and parked the remaining $98.5 million in USD cash. It also spent around $208 million buying back about 2.1 million shares of its STRC preferred . Strategy spent much of the year leaning on preferred issuance to fund purchases, and the company is now using the buyback to tidy up its preferred stack while still adding coins. Saylor teased the purchase Sunday with his usual tracker chart and a line that made the rounds on X: “We found room for even more orange.” The buy landed a few days after Strategy reported its third-quarter results on Thursday. Net income hit $19.5 billion, up from $2.79 billion a year earlier, driven by a $20.9 billion operating gain tied to the bitcoin price rising during the quarter. That gain is a paper one under fair-value accounting, not cash. Saylor called it the start of the next bitcoin bull market and pointed to bitcoin trading about 21% above its 200-week moving average. The same release said CFO Andrew Kang will step down November 5, with COO Reza Virasteh taking over the role in January. Strategy shareholders also recently approved a proposal allowing four preferred stocks — STRF, STRC, STRK, and STRD — to accrue dividends daily, including weekends and holidays, with 99.3% of votes cast in favor. The change was intended to improve liquidity, reduce reinvestment delays, and increase price stability, while keeping dividend rates and total obligations unchanged. The new payment schedule remained subject to board approval and regulatory filings, with implementation expected to begin in November 2026 for STRC and January 2027 for the other preferred stocks. BREAKING: Public companies Strive and Strategy bought a combined 934 Bitcoin worth $72.6 million. Strategy: 810 BTC Strive: 124 BTC pic.twitter.com/ObXGCz7weH — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 2, 2026 Strive adds bitcoin as well Strive is still in the race for second place among public holders. The Matt Cole-run firm added 124 BTC between October 24 and 30 at about $80,526 each, lifting its stack to 43,124 BTC. That’s a smaller buy than its previous week, when it added more than 6,000 coins, but Cole has been consistent about his approach. item.title: Frozen part II: Hackers remotely defrost produce in Euro supermarkets ... again
item.description: The cyberattacks on commercial refrigerators and freezers in Europe continue, as a slew of grocery stores in Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden report widespread food wastage as a result of miscreants raising the temperatures to highs of 50ºC (122°F). In Belgium, around 40 Delhaize stores were affected after the attackers reportedly switched fridges and freezers into defrost mode overnight, between Sunday and Monday, resulting in stock issues. Diego Louwers, a Proxy Delhaize store manager in Overijse, near Brussels, told RTL Info that the consequences of the cyberattacks were "catastrophic," forcing the store to throw out the entirety of its fresh and frozen products. "We can't have anything worse in our line of work," he said. "We have to throw away all of our merchandise, and it's both heartbreaking and very complicated operationally." A Delhaize spokesperson said it took steps to ensure stores remain stocked, although fresh and frozen products are "temporarily somewhat limited." "On Monday, 2 November, we identified an IT incident affecting the refrigeration systems in several dozen of our stores," they said. "We immediately took the necessary measures to keep our stores operational and ensure that our customers can continue to do their shopping as usual. "In the affected stores, the range of fresh and frozen products is temporarily somewhat limited. Our distribution centres are operating normally, and there has been no disruption to deliveries to our stores. "We are, of course, continuing to ensure that our products are stored and presented under optimal conditions, so that we can provide our customers with the quality and freshness they have come to expect from us." Around 15 Carrefour stores are also reportedly affected, as are sites operated by Intermarché, Spar, and Shop & Go stores located at Q8 service stations. Belgium’s De Laet & Van Haver chain of butcher shops reported temperature rises in its appliances too, but followed up with a statement on Monday saying there was no impact on its produce, and all stores remain open. Simultaneously, similar issues have affected Swedish grocery chain ICA, which confirmed attacks on a "small number of stores." "We can confirm that we have been informed of an incident overnight affecting a small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA’s central network," a company spokesperson said. "The incident impacted the stores’ refrigeration and freezer systems. ICA is currently supporting the affected stores in managing the situation." ICA did not respond to questions about the scale of food wastage nor when normal operations are expected to continue. One store, ICA Nära in Böda on Öland, said via social media that it is open today but has no fresh or frozen produce to sell. "Unfortunately, we are one of the stores whose refrigerators and freezers have been hacked," it said. "We are open as usual, but unfortunately we have no refrigerators and freezers to sell. item.title: 'VisionQuest' homework guide: Everything you need to watch to understand Marvel's WandaVision follow-up
item.description: null Marvel Studios' existential superhero series " VisionQuest " has arrived on Disney+, and we've already been treated to four intriguing episodes that delve into the complex life of Vision, Paul Bettany's intelligent android and former card-carrying member of The Avengers. The staggered storyline leading up to this show began with 2021's " WandaVision " and the 2024 follow-up, "Agatha All Along," with Marvel Studios proclaiming "VisionQuest" to be "the final vision of the groundbreaking trilogy." So, for those trying to catch up on current events in this trilogy of MCU shows starring Vision, and to avoid any lingering confusion, let’s take a step back to fill in the gaps. And now, this isn't as simple as just "watch all the Marvel movies and shows in order," because that is a frankly ridiculous undertaking and entirely too much homework to do before watching a show. We're distilling it down to just what you need to know to understand VisionQuest. Spoiler warning: It should go without saying, but there are spoilers for previous Marvel movies and shows in this article. You have been warned! TLDR: Marvel shows and movies you need to watch ahead of VisionQuest We'll go into some detail on all the connections below, but if you just want a list of the essential Marvel shows and movies to watch before VisionQuest, here it is. Note that this is just the essentials. There are loads of small references to other movies and shows in the MCU, but they're just nods. Avengers: Age of Ultron Avengers: Infinity War WandaVision Doctor Strange and the Multiverse of Madness* Agatha All Along *This one is debatable. It continues Wanda's story from WandaVision, but it's not really essential for understanding the events of VisionQuest. Both are the true vision. Neither is the true Vision (Image credit: Disney / Marvel) We kick things off with 2018's "Avengers: Infinity War," where the mighty Thanos murdered Vision by plucking out his golden, forehead-mounted Mind Stone for his Infinity Gauntlet. From that moment forward, Vision was dead, and Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) was cast into unfathomable grief and not-so-repressed anger. From there, we pick up the story in the 2021 Disney+ series "WandaVision." Set weeks after "Avengers: Endgame," this show features two separate versions of Vision. One was a new synthezoid version, Frankensteined together from the components of the old Vision by S.W.O.R.D., nicknamed White Vision. The other Vision is a supernatural manifestation, brought to life via Wanda Maximoff’s sorcery; he is known as Hex Vision. White Vision is ready to rumble in "VisionQuest" (Image credit: Disney+) So, which of these two Visions appears in "VisionQuest"? That's the fun (and confusing) part, because the answer is both of them. At the end of "WandaVision," Hex Vision restores the lost memories of White Vision, essentially merging two entities into one. So, the Vision we see in "VisionQuest" is the physical body of White Vision, injected with thoug
